 Home / Cannabis 101 / How to Accurately Measure Tincture Oils 
 

 How to Accurately Measure Tincture Oils
 Working in cannabis retail for the past two years, I’ve talked to many people who purchase tincture oils, get them home, and have no idea how to dose themselves correctly. Many know how many milligrams of THC they’d like to take, but just aren’t sure how to get there. This is because the dropper is typically measured in milliliters, which simply tells you how much liquid you are intaking rather than mgs of THC. The process to getting there is very simple once you break it down.
 
 First, figure out how many milligrams are in the entire bottle. Now you are going to divide that number by the number of milliliters in the entire bottle. The number you get is how many milligrams are in a full 1ml dropper. Remember that concentration varies between different brands and sizes of bottles so it’s smart to double check your math with each tincture you purchase. I have one bottle at home that contains 4 milligrams in a full dropper, while another is 15 milligrams. Quite a variance.
 
 Example: 530 mgs THC total / 60 ml of liquid in bottle = 8.8 mgs of THC in a full 1 ml dropper. So if you take a 5 mg dose, you’d use slightly more than half the dropper.

Intro to Cannabis 101 and Things to Know about Cannabis

 Whether you’re new to cannabis, returning after some time away, or simply looking to better understand today’s products, Cannabis 101 is a great place to start . This introductory guide covers the fundamentals of cannabis in clear, easy to understand language, helping you learn about cannabinoids, terpenes, common product types, consumption methods, responsible use, and what to consider when choosing cannabis. At Cape Cod Cannabis, we believe that better information leads to more confident decisions, and our knowledgeable team in Wellfleet is always here to help answer your questions along the way.

 A quick 2-minute cannabis introduction for you...

 

 Click the Intro to Cannabis 101 links below to view:

 
 
 
 Cannnabis 101 - Digital Edition 
 
 

 
 
 
 Intro to Cannabis 101 (Digital Edition) 
 
 

 
 
 
 FREE Educational Rack Cards for Cape Cod 
 
 

 
 
 
 Intro to Cannabis 101 (English PDF) 
 
 

 
 
 
 Intro to Cannabis 101 (Spanish PDF) 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 Intro to Cannabis 101 

 
 
 

 What Should I Know About Cannabis?

 Cannabis is first of all a plant, and today it comes in many different varieties and forms. What is unique about cannabis is the combination of its essential oils: terpenes and cannabinoids . While terpenes can be found on many other plants, only the cannabis plant has cannabinoids.
 
 Cannabinoids have a medicinal effect by imitating compounds our bodies naturally produce (endocannabinoids). Together the cannabinoids and terpenes hold most of the influence when it comes to the effects of cannabis.
 
 There are over 85 cannabinoids in cannabis, but the main two that you should know about are THC and CBD:
 

 THC

 (DELTA-9-TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL)
 THC is responsible for the psychoactive (“stoned”) effects. Commonly experienced effects include euphoria, relaxation, and “giggles”.

 
 
 
 Shop Flower 
 
 

 CBD

 (CANNABIDIOL)
 CBD has little to no psychoactive effects and can balance or counteract the anxiety produced by THC. CBD can reduce anxiety, provide pain relief, suppress nausea, support cardiovascular health, and have anti-inflammatory properties.

 
 
 
 Shop CBD 
 
 

 
 
 
 Learn about Cannabinoids 
 
 

 
 
 

 What are cannabis Strain Types?

 SATIVA

 Increases energy, focus, elevates mood, increases creativity.
 Consumed during Daytime.
 
 
 
 
 Shop Sativa 
 
 

 INDICA

 Relaxes and reduces stress, pain, and anxiety, promotes sleep and reduces inflammation.
 Consumed at Nighttime.
 
 
 
 
 Shop Indica 
 
 

 
 Remember: Most cannabis strains are HYBRIDS and their effect fall somewhere between the two.
 
 All products vary in their strength of effect on body and mid. Each person is unique and may experience cannabis differently. Read the packaging label for product laboratory results and consumption suggestions. Always start with a small dose and wait until getting another one.
 

 
 
 
 Learn more about Strain Types 
 
 

 
 
 

 What are Terpenes?

 We also mentioned terpenes which are aromatic oils that distinguish cannabis varieties with smell and flavor, but they also affect the human body in a variety of ways and contribute to the Entourage Effect.
 
 Did you know? These are the 5 things that are chemically similar to a cannabis high: Catnip; Running; Love; Chocolate; Cheese.
 
 Most common terpenes are Pinene, Myrcene, Limonene, Caryophyllene, Linalool, Humulene .
 
 Cannabis can be classified into two categories based on its effects:

 
 
 
 Learn about Terpenes 
 
 

 
 
 

 WHICH CANNABIS PRODUCTS TO CHOOSE?
 The effects of the cannabis products will vary significantly depending on the individual as each person metabolizes, processes and experiences marijuana differently. Before making a purchase, you should understand your desired effect, its lengths and strength of impact as well as the overall experience that you are looking for. Our expert Product Specialists will help you find the right product based on the following factors:
 
 Type: we offer flower , edibles , vaporizers , concentrates , topicals and tinctures – all of which are consumed in different ways.
 Dosage: products come in a variety of strengths and dosages. You might want to start with a low dosage, especially if you are new to cannabis.
 Effect: the main groups of cannabis strains are Indica (sedative/relaxing), Sativa (invigorating/uplifting) and Hybrids (fall in between Indica and Sativa). Keep in mind that terpenes will also influence the effect of the product.
 
 UNDERSTANDING THE DAILY PURCHASE LIMIT IN MA FOR RECREATIONAL CANNABIS
 Massachusetts has a well-defined legal framework for recreational cannabis purchases to ensure consumer safety, responsible usage, and regulatory compliance. The daily legal limit is 56 grams (2 ounces) of flower , but this can be distributed across various cannabis products.
 
 Click here for more information and an online calculator to determine your daily purchase per category.
 
 WHAT TYPE OF CANNABIS PRODUCT AND METHOD OF USE IS RIGHT FOR ME?
 There are many ways to use cannabis, and its effect may vary depending on the method. If you are not sure what works best for you – ask our Product Specialist about the products and methods of use.

 To choose the correct product you may consult with our Product Specialist who will recommend the best type of product and method of consumption based on your preference and desired effect.

 
 
 

 WHAT IS THE CORRECT CANNABIS DOSAGE?
 All products vary in their strength of effect on body and mind, and cannabinoid profile. Strain specific details are labeled on all products after they are tested by certified third-party laboratories. It is important that anyone using marijuana is careful in finding the appropriate dose for their desired effects. Each person is unique and may experience cannabis differently.
 
 Before using cannabis re-read the laboratory test results and instructions on the packaging label. This will help you understand how strong the product is and what is the recommended method and dosage of use. It is always best to start with a small dosage and wait a few hours to realize the full effects. Most products come in a variety of strengths and dosages, so start low and go slow, especially if you are new to cannabis or trying out a new product.
 
 Remember:
 
 Wait 15-20 minutes before taking another inhalation of a flower or
 For sublingual use wait 30-60 minutes before taking another
 Always have some food before taking an Edible and remember to keep your dose within 5mg. Never rush for an additional dose, wait at least 2 hours before consuming more.
 
 Always note the time when you used the product to keep track of the onset and duration.
 
 If you are not into math: cannabis is often in grams or ounces. To better understand the weight of our products please use the following conversion table:
 
 3.5g ≈ 1/8 oz. | 7g ≈ 1/4 oz. | 14g ≈ 1/2 oz. | 28g ≈ 1 oz. | 56g ≈ 2 ozs. 
 
 Note: All conversions are approximate and have been rounded up or down to the nearest whole number. 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 Important Information about Cannabis

 All information contained herein and, on our website, www.capecodcannabis.com, is for educational purposes only. None of this information should be interpreted as medical or treatment advice for any person or condition. Always consult with a licensed physician in all matters regarding your health.
 
 The information provided on this website does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice; instead, all information, content, and materials available on this site are for general informational purposes only. Information on this website may not constitute the most up-to-date legal or other information. This website contains links to other third-party websites.
 
 Such links are only for the convenience of the reader, user or browser; the ABA and its members do not recommend or endorse the contents of the third-party sites.

 ALCOHOL. Do not mix cannabis with alcohol.
 CONSUMPTION . Cannabis use is allowed only in a private space where smoking and/or vaping is allowed. Consumption is prohibited in or around the Cape Cod Cannabis location. Do not consume in public areas as it is prohibited by State and Local laws. Consumption and possession of cannabis on the territory of the Cape Cod National Seashore and the Cape Cod Rail Trail is prohibited. Violators will be put on “blacklist” and would not be able to shop at Cape Cod Cannabis locations in the future.
 DIVERSION . Consumer may not sell marijuana to any other individual or distribute to minors, doing so may impose a fine and/or imprisonment; Violators will be put on “blacklist” and would not be able to shop at Cape Cod Cannabis locations in the future. Any unused, excess, or contaminated product can be returned to the dispensary for disposal.
 DOSAGE always speaking with your doctor about your medical history and the medications you are taking before using cannabis. Consult with a physician regarding dosage. For consumers who are new to cannabis we recommend starting with smallest dosage according to package directions and allowing sufficient time to pass to allow effects to be felt, based on the method of consumption or application. Some people report dry mouth, dizziness or paranoia when using cannabis. While many use cannabis to combat anxiety, it may create anxiety in others. Responsible dosing can help you avoid unpleasant experiences with cannabis.
 DRIVING & MACHINERY cannabis can slow your reaction time. Under M.G.L. c90, §24 it is illegal to drive or operate machinery under the influence of marijuana. When driving, keep your cannabis in a secure area of your vehicle, out of reach of the driver and passengers.
 FOOD. Do not consume cannabis infused products (edibles) on an empty stomach. We recommend eating a full meal before consuming cannabis infused products as it helps lower the intensity of effects. The undesirable effect will subside with time.
 LIMITS. You may purchase up to 2 ounces of cannabis flower or up to 10 grams of cannabis concentrate per day. Possessing more than the legal limit (2 oz. of Flower or each flower equivalency) outside of your place of residence may be penalized up to 6 months imprisonment or a $500 fine.
 PENALTIES. For information regarding penalties for possession or distribution of marijuana in violation of Massachusetts law please refer to M.G.L. c94G, §13 . Selling cannabis to others is illegal and a first offense (under 50 lbs.) can be punishable up to 2 years of imprisonment or a $5,000 fine.
 PREGNANCY certain health risks may be associated with consumption of cannabis while pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant.
 STATE BORDER. Stay in Massachusetts and do not cross state lines with cannabis products.
 STORAGE . Store cannabis securely, away from children and pets. Keep cannabis in the original child-proof packaging and away from other food items. To keep cannabis fresh, store in dark, dry and cool place.
 TOO MUCH OR TOO STRONG? Anxiety and paranoia may accompany accidental overdose. It is best to stay calm and remain in a comfortable and safe place.
 TOLERANCE, DEPENDENCE AND WITHDRAWAL . Although it is generally accepted that cannabis is not a physically addictive substance, a psychological dependence is possible with excessive usage of any substance.
 
 Please consume cannabis and cannabis products at your own risk. If you or someone you know is experiencing symptoms of substance abuse, consider talking to someone, your physician our counselor, about the drug use.
 
 Some examples of symptoms and signs of substance abuse are:
 Neglecting responsibilities at school, work, or home because of drug use.
 Using drugs under dangerous conditions or taking risks while high.
 Built up a drug tolerance.
 Taking drugs to avoid or relieve withdrawal symptoms. Symptoms may include nausea, sweating, shakiness, and extreme anxiety.
 Causing problems in relationships.
 Abandoning previously enjoyed activities.
 Continuing using drugs, despite knowing it is hurting you.
 Losing control over drug use, may want to stop using, but feel powerless.
 Experiencing legal trouble, such as arrests for disorderly conduct, driving under the influence, or stealing to support a drug habit.
 If you or someone you know is exhibiting signs or symptoms of substance abuse please contact the Massachusetts substance abuse helpline at (800) 327-5050 for further assistance 
 
 DO’s 
 DO take your cannabis products directly from the dispensary to a private residence.
 DO keep your cannabis sealed and out of reach while in your motor vehicle. Cannabis cannot be transported once opened.
 DO store cannabis in a safe place away from direct sunlight and out of reach of any children or pets.
 DO consult your physician if you have any medical conditions before using cannabis.
 DON’Ts 
 Do NOT consume cannabis in public.
 Do NOT drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence of cannabis.
 Do NOT consume cannabis with alcohol. Cannabis may increase the intensity of intoxication.
 Do NOT consume cannabis on National Seashore and bike trail.
 Do NOT travel out of the state of Massachusetts with your cannabis.
 Do NOT engage in the diversion of any marijuana products.
 
 How Much Weed Can I Buy at a Time? 
2 ounces of flower or 10 grams of concentrate. Up to 1000mg of edibles at a time, which can be up to 200 milligrams of THC. Please visit our Understanding the Daily Purchase Limit in MA page to calculate.
 
 How Much Am I Allowed to Possess? 
You’re allowed to hold up to ten ounces of marijuana in your home. If you’re on the street, the 2 ounce or 10 gram rule still applies. You also can’t go out in public, or drive around in your vehicle, with an open container of weed. This will earn you a fine of $500, so respect the law and keep it sealed up.

 CLICK TO VIEW FAQs
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Where is Cape Cod Cannabis located? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Recreational Dispensary is located at 1446 US-6, Wellfleet, MA 02667 . We’re conveniently located along Route 6 in the South Wellfleet shopping plaza, designed like a rest stop, for easy entry and exit with plenty of free parking, includes a bakery, liquor store, and U.S. Post Office for your convenience. Click here for directions . 
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis is a licensed adult-use recreational dispensary serving residents and visitors alike in Barnstable , Bourne , Brewster , Chatham , Dennis , Eastham , Falmouth , Harwich , Hyannis , Mashpee , Orleans , Provincetown , Sandwich , Truro , Wellfleet , Yarmouth and beyond. 

 
 
 
 
 
 Where can I find weed near me on Cape Cod? 
 If you’re searching for weed near me on Cape Cod , Cape Cod Cannabis is an adult-use recreational dispensary located at 1446 US-6 in Wellfleet, Massachusetts , in the South Wellfleet area of the Outer Cape. We’re open daily and offer a wide selection of recreational cannabis products. Customers 21+ can shop in-store or order online for convenient pickup with valid ID.

 
 
 
 
 
 What is the legal age to purchase cannabis in Massachusetts? 
 We welcome anyone 21 years of age or older with a valid Government ID (e.g., Drivers License, Passport, etc.) to verify your age upon entry. Unfortunately, we cannot accept expired MA ID’s unless, when already renewed, you bring the expired MA ID with the actual MA RMV documentation for the renewal.
 
 Unfortunately, we cannot accept any out-of-state or International ID’s that are expired. 
 
 Note : We respect if you are wearing a mask when you enter but please know that, per regulations, we have to properly identify everyone who enters. You will be asked to momentarily remove (or lower) your mask for identification purposes. We thank you for your cooperation and understanding. 

 
 
 
 
 
 What should I expect when visiting a dispensary for the first time? 
 If it’s your first time visiting a dispensary in Massachusetts, the process is simple and welcoming. When you arrive, you’ll be asked to show a valid government-issued ID to confirm you are 21 or older. After check-in, you can browse the menu or speak with a knowledgeable staff member (often called a budtender) who can help you choose products based on your preferences and experience level.
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis, you’ll find a variety of options including flower , pre-rolls , edibles , vapes , tinctures , topicals , CBD and concentrates . Our budtenders are here to answer questions and make recommendations, whether you’re looking to relax, sleep better, or try cannabis for the first time. Once you’ve made your selection, you’ll proceed to checkout—we accept cash and debit payment options. We also have an on-site ATM for your convenience.
 
 Overall, expect a safe, regulated, and educational experience designed to help you feel comfortable and informed…and NOT rushed.
 
 We also offer an online assistant (bottom left side of the website) to ask questions and lead you in the right direction. Please give us a call at (774) 383-3133 if you have further questions.

 
 
 
 
 
 What do customers say about Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 
 2026 Cape Cod Choice Awards: Best CBD Store Winner | Top 3 Best Cannabis Dispensary 
 Customers frequently mention our knowledgeable and friendly team, wide cannabis selection, personalized service, welcoming atmosphere, convenient Route 6 location, and overall dispensary experience. Read our recent customer reviews to see feedback directly from customers.

 
 
 
 
 
 Can I leave a review for Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 Yes. Visit our Leave Your Review page to share your experience on Google or Yelp.

 
 
 
 
 
 What are the operating hours for Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 We’re open 7 days a week. Please check our hours for the most up-to-date hours, including holiday schedules.

 
 
 
 
 
 What cannabis products do you carry? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Dispensary in Wellfleet offers the largest selection of quality flower , pre-rolls , seeds , edibles , vapes , concentrates , syrups / tinctures , CBD , topicals , pet drops and more at the BEST prices on Cape Cod…something for every preference and experience level. Always worth the trip! 

 
 
 
 
 
 Is there a limit to how much cannabis I can buy? 
 Yes. As of April 19, 2026 , Massachusetts law allows you to purchase up to 2 ounces of flower (Recreational) or its equivalent in other cannabis products per day.
 
 Click here to visit our “Understanding the Daily Purchase Limit in MA” page for more information and to calculate your daily purchase.
 
 Recreational = 56 grams (flower) a day is the legal MA limit, which can constitute: 
 
 • Flower : Up to 56 grams (2 ounces).
 • Edibles : A total of 10 00mg THC , which is roughly 10 packs of 20 servings , each serving containing 5mg of THC .
 • Concentrates : Up to 10 grams of cannabis concentrates, such as wax, shatter, or live resin (equivalent to 10 x 1g or 20 x 0.5g packages).
 • Tinctures : A total of 10000mg = approximately 10 x 1000mg bottles , depending on the product’s potency and total THC content.
 • Pre-roll Joints : 56 pre-roll joints , assuming each joint contains roughly 1 gram of flower .
 • Vape Cartridges : Up to 20 x 0.5g cartridges or 10 x 1g cartridges/disposables .
 
 CBD = No Limit 
 Topicals = No Limit 
 Accessories = No Limit 

 
 
 
 
 
 Are your cannabis products tested for safety and quality? 
 Yes. Cannabis products sold at Cape Cod Cannabis are required to meet Massachusetts testing and labeling requirements before being offered for retail sale.

 
 
 
 
 
 What payment methods are accepted? 
 We accept cash, debit cards and CanPay . A regular ATM is also located on-site for your convenience.
 
 Note : ATM and Debit transactions will incur a small third-party merchant fee. 

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you offer online ordering or pre-orders? 
 Yes! Browse our full menu online or our Daily Offers page and place a pre-order for quick and easy pickup in-store.
 
 Once you finalize your order, it will be filled within 15 minutes and you will be able to pick it up at the store. Changes to pre-orders can be made during checkout at the store.
 
 PLEASE double check your phone number when entering your pre-order. 
 
 We will not keep orders placed, past our store closing, the day of when the order was placed.

 
 
 
 
 
 What should I know about cannabis? 
 For a quick overview of the different types of cannabis products, terpenes, cannabinoids, strains and more please visit Intro to Cannabis 101 .

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you offer a Loyalty Program? 
 Yes! We do offer a FREE Loyalty VIP Program where you can accumulate points that will be generated automatically and tracked for you for redemption.
 
 NOTE : Per MA Cannabis Control Commission regulations, Loyalty Points CANNOT be used for cannabis products . 
 
 Currently, y ou CAN use your Loyalty Points toward Cape Cod Cannabis CBD, Accessories or Merch only. 
 
 As soon as the CCC ( Cannabis Control Commission ) will approve or will remove the limitations on the promotions, you will be able to use these points toward all Cape Cod Cannabis products. That way you will not miss out on any points you could have accumulated if there were no limitations to begin with. In the meantime, you will get access to the VIP program.
 
 Not a Loyalty Program VIP member? JOIN FOR FREE IN-STORE TODAY! 
 
 Already a Loyalty Program VIP member? Click here to Shop your Loyalty VIP Points. 

 
 
 
 
 
 What is your Return Policy? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis is committed to customer satisfaction when it comes to the products we sell.
 
 RETURN POLICY 
 Please visit our Return Policy page for more information.
 
 CONTACT US 
 If you have any questions regarding our Return Policy please contact us or call (774) 383-3133.

 
 
 
 
 
 What is your Privacy Policy? 
 PRIVACY POLICY 
 Please visit our Privacy Policy page for more information.
 
 CONTACT US 
 If you have any questions regarding this Privacy Policy please contact us or call us at (774) 383-3133.

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you ship your Apparel? 
 Yes! Our apparel, hats, beanies, sweatshirts, joggers and more can be shipped to you (within the United States only) via USPS Priority. Please visit our online store Blue Tail Apparel & Merch @ www.BlueTail.cc for convenient, safe and easy shopping and we will ship your order to you!
 
 Of course, you can always pre-order Cape Cod Cannabis apparel , accessories and merch for local pickup.

 In-store or pre-order (non-cannabis) purchases on CapeCodCannabis.com are applicable using your Loyalty Points.

 Labor Day Weekend on Cape Cod 2026

 
 
 
 
 
 September 4, 2026 
 
 

 Home / Cape Cod Lifestyle / Labor Day Weekend on Cape Cod 2026 
 

 
 Labor Day Weekend on Cape Cod 2026: Things to Do in Wellfleet & the Outer Cape
 Labor Day Weekend on Cape Cod is one of the best times to experience the Outer Cape. The summer energy is still here, the beaches are beautiful, local restaurants and shops are open, and Wellfleet is packed with live music, art, food, outdoor activities, and events to help celebrate the unofficial end of summer.
 
 In 2026, Labor Day falls on Monday, September 7 , creating a long weekend from Friday, September 4 through Monday, September 7.
 If you’re planning a Cape Cod Labor Day Weekend getaway , here’s what’s happening around Wellfleet and the Outer Cape, including the Outer Cape Music Festival , Wellfleet Firsts, gallery events, live entertainment, nature activities, and more.
 
 And for adults 21+ who choose to make cannabis part of their Cape Cod weekend, we’ll also tell you where to find Cape Cod Cannabis in South Wellfleet and our End of Summer Blowout Offers .
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 Shop Our End of Summer Blowout Offers 
 
 

 
 What Is Happening on Cape Cod for Labor Day Weekend 2026?
 
 Outer Cape Music Festival – September 5 & 6
 
 One of the biggest events in Wellfleet this Labor Day Weekend is the 4th Annual Outer Cape Music Festival , taking place Saturday, September 5 and Sunday, September 6 at Wellfleet Town Pier .
 
 The festival runs from 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM and combines live music, food, vendors, oysters, family activities, waterfront views, and charitable giving. The 2026 festival features headliners Electric Six and Crooked Coast , along with regional and Cape Cod performers. Festival profits support charitable organizations and programs serving the community.
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis is proud to sponsor the 2026 Outer Cape Music Festival and support an event that brings music, visitors, residents, local businesses, and charitable organizations together in Wellfleet.
 
 If live music is part of your Labor Day plans, this should be near the top of your list. For more Outer Cape Music Festival 2026 information and buy tickets click here! 
 
 
 
 Explore Wellfleet Firsts & the Saturday Gallery Stroll
 Saturday evening offers even more reasons to spend time in downtown Wellfleet.
 
 Wellfleet Firsts takes place on Saturday, September 5, creating a walkable celebration from Main Street to the Marina. Local shops stay open later while galleries throughout the Wellfleet Cultural District participate in evening events and receptions.
 
 The Wellfleet Gallery Stroll also runs from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM , giving visitors an opportunity to explore galleries, discover new artwork, meet artists, and support local businesses. The stroll is free.
 
 There is also a free family art demonstration scheduled on the Town Hall lawn from 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM, weather permitting.
 
 It’s a great complement to the music festival and another way to experience the creative side of Wellfleet. Visit Wellfleet Cultural District and Events for more information. 
 
 
 
 Taste, Toast & Roast at Wellfleet Preservation Hall
 Start the holiday weekend a little early on Friday, September 4 with Taste, Toast & Roast , celebrating 15 years of arts, culture, and community at Wellfleet Preservation Hall.
 
 The event runs from 4:30 PM to 7:00 PM and brings together local chefs, restaurants, beverages, live music, and community. The evening includes a cocktail hour, appetizers, raw bar, tapas under the tent, entertainment, and auctions supporting the Hall.
 
 It’s an excellent way to kick off Labor Day Weekend while experiencing some of the food, culture, and community that make the Outer Cape unique. Visit Wellfleet Cultural District and Events for more information. 
 
 
 
 Catch the Final Weekend of Cirque by the Sea
 Looking for something different or a family friendly activity?
 
 Cirque by the Sea: Summer in the City reaches the end of its summer run during Labor Day Weekend. The production features acrobatics, aerialists, juggling, theater, and comedy under the Big Top at Wellfleet Harbor Actors Theater.
 
 A Sunday performance is scheduled for September 6 at 4:00 PM , making it another option for families visiting Wellfleet over the holiday weekend. Visit Wellfleet Cultural District and Events for more information. 
 
 
 
 Discover the Natural Side of Wellfleet
 Labor Day Weekend doesn’t need to revolve entirely around scheduled events.
 
 Some of the best things to do in Wellfleet don’t require a stage or ticket.
 
 Spend part of the weekend enjoying the beaches, walking trails, ponds, salt marshes, and spectacular landscapes of the Outer Cape.
 
 Mass Audubon Wellfleet Bay Wildlife Sanctuary also has September nature programming, including birding, shorebird programs, nature activities, and other opportunities to experience the Cape’s wildlife and coastal environment.
 
 Or simply pack a beach bag, explore the Cape Cod National Seashore, walk around Wellfleet Harbor, and enjoy one more long summer weekend near the water. Visit Wellfleet Cultural District and Events for more information. 
 
 
 
 Browse the Wellfleet Flea Market
 Another classic Cape Cod activity is Wellfleet Flea Market on Route 6.
 
 The market is scheduled from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM Saturday and Sunday , making it an easy morning stop before heading to the beach, downtown Wellfleet, or the Outer Cape Music Festival later in the day.
 
 You never quite know what you’re going to find, which is part of the fun.
 
 
 
 Are There Labor Day Parades Near Wellfleet?
 If you’re specifically searching for a Labor Day parade on Cape Cod , there does not currently appear to be a major parade scheduled in Wellfleet for Labor Day Weekend 2026.
 
 The nearby Eastham Windmill Weekend Parade is happening the following weekend, on Sunday, September 13 at 10:00 AM . This year’s theme is “Eastham Rocks!” , and the parade travels from Old Orchard Road to Windmill Green. Visit Eastham Windmill Weekend for more information. 
 
 If you’re staying on Cape Cod beyond Labor Day Weekend, it’s another Outer Cape tradition worth checking out.
 
 
 
 Why Visit Cape Cod for Labor Day Weekend?
 Labor Day Weekend occupies a sweet spot in the Cape Cod calendar.
 
 You can still enjoy the energy of summer, but September begins bringing a different rhythm to the Outer Cape.
 
 Spend your weekend:
 
 Relaxing on a Cape Cod beach 
 Exploring the Cape Cod National Seashore 
 Walking around Wellfleet Harbor 
 Discovering local art galleries 
 Enjoying seafood and local restaurants 
 Shopping at locally owned businesses 
 Listening to live music 
 Exploring trails and wildlife 
 Catching an Outer Cape sunset 
 Attending the Outer Cape Music Festival 
 
 It’s one last opportunity to celebrate summer before Cape Cod settles into the quieter pace of fall.
 
 
 
 Visiting a Cannabis Dispensary on Cape Cod This Labor Day Weekend?
 For adults 21 and older (with a VALID ID) who choose to include cannabis in their Labor Day Weekend plans, stop by Cape Cod Cannabis Recreational Dispensary in South Wellfleet .
 
 Located at 1446 US-6, Wellfleet, MA 02667 , we’re conveniently located for visitors traveling through Wellfleet, Eastham, Truro, Provincetown, Orleans, and the surrounding Outer Cape.
 
 End of Summer Blowout Offers
 Labor Day Weekend is also a great time to take advantage of our End of Summer Blowout Offers & Every day Offers at Cape Cod Cannabis .
 
 Explore our huge selection of: 
 
 Cannabis Flower 
 Pre-rolls 
 Edibles 
 Vape products 
 Concentrates 
 Tinctures 
 CBD products 
 Topicals 
 Seeds 
 Accessories 
 Apparel 
 
 With the largest selection of quality cannabis products and the best prices on Cape Cod , our knowledgeable team can help you explore different products, answer questions, and make informed choices based on your preferences.
 
 Whether you’re heading north toward Provincetown, spending the weekend in Wellfleet, visiting the National Seashore, or going to the Outer Cape Music Festival, Cape Cod Cannabis is an easy stop along Route 6 in the South Wellfleet shopping plaza with plenty of free parking.
 
 Open daily from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM. 
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis…Always Worth the Trip! 
 
 
 
 Cannabis & Labor Day Weekend: Know Before You Go
 If you’re visiting from outside Massachusetts, remember that recreational cannabis is available to adults 21+ with valid identification , but purchasing cannabis doesn’t mean it can be consumed anywhere.
 
 Cannabis consumption is not permitted at the Outer Cape Music Festival or in public places , and you should never drive while impaired.
 
 Cannabis also cannot legally be transported across state lines. If you’re visiting from another state, anything purchased in Massachusetts needs to remain in Massachusetts.
 
 Enjoy Cape Cod responsibly and plan ahead.
 
 
 
 Plan Your Labor Day Weekend in Wellfleet
 If you’re wondering what to do on Cape Cod for Labor Day Weekend 2026 , Wellfleet makes an excellent home base.
 
 Come for the beaches. Stay for the art, restaurants, music, local businesses, waterfront scenery, and laid back Outer Cape atmosphere.
 
 Catch the Outer Cape Music Festival September 5 and 6 , explore the Wellfleet Gallery Stroll and Wellfleet Firsts, experience local food and culture, spend some time outdoors, and enjoy one more taste of summer before fall arrives.
 
 And if cannabis is part of your weekend, visit Cape Cod Cannabis in South Wellfleet , explore our End of Summer Blowout Offers , and discover why we’re Always Worth the Trip! 
 
 
 
 Frequently Asked Questions About Labor Day Weekend on Cape Cod
 
 When is Labor Day Weekend 2026 on Cape Cod?
 Labor Day is Monday, September 7, 2026 , with the main holiday weekend running September 5–7.
 
 What are the best things to do in Wellfleet for Labor Day Weekend?
 Highlights include the Outer Cape Music Festival, Wellfleet Firsts, the Gallery Stroll, Cirque by the Sea, beaches, galleries, restaurants, Wellfleet Harbor, nature activities, and the Cape Cod National Seashore.
 
 When is the Outer Cape Music Festival 2026?
 The Outer Cape Music Festival takes place September 5 and 6, 2026 at Wellfleet Town Pier , with music scheduled from 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM.
 
 Is Cape Cod Cannabis near the Outer Cape Music Festival?
 Yes. Cape Cod Cannabis is located at 1446 US-6, Wellfleet, MA 02667 in the South Wellfleet shopping plaza , making it a convenient stop when traveling to or from Wellfleet and other Outer Cape destinations.
 
 Is Cape Cod Cannabis open on Labor Day Weekend?
 Cape Cod Cannabis is open daily from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM , including Monday September 7th.
 
 
 
 Always worth the trip!

Learn about Cannabis

 Learn about Cannabis and other important information

 
 
 

 All information contained herein and, on our website, www.capecodcannabis.com, is for educational purposes only. None of this information should be interpreted as medical or treatment advice for any person or condition. Always consult with a licensed physician in all matters regarding your health.
 
 The information provided on this website does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice; instead, all information, content, and materials available on this site are for general informational purposes only. Information on this website may not constitute the most up-to-date legal or other information. This website contains links to other third-party websites. Such links are only for the convenience of the reader, user or browser; the ABA and its members do not recommend or endorse the contents of the third-party sites.

 
 
 

 ALCOHOL. Do not mix cannabis with alcohol.
 CONSUMPTION . Cannabis use is allowed only in a private space where smoking and/or vaping is allowed. Consumption is prohibited in or around the Cape Cod Cannabis location. Do not consume in public areas as it is prohibited by State and Local laws. Consumption and possession of cannabis on the territory of the Cape Cod National Seashore and the Cape Cod Rail Trail is prohibited. Violators will be put on “blacklist” and would not be able to shop at Cape Cod Cannabis locations in the future.
 DIVERSION . Consumer may not sell marijuana to any other individual or distribute to minors, doing so may impose a fine and/or imprisonment; Violators will be put on “blacklist” and would not be able to shop at Cape Cod Cannabis locations in the future. Any unused, excess, or contaminated product can be returned to the dispensary for disposal.
 DOSAGE always speaking with your doctor about your medical history and the medications you are taking before using cannabis. Consult with a physician regarding dosage. For consumers who are new to cannabis we recommend starting with smallest dosage according to package directions and allowing sufficient time to pass to allow effects to be felt, based on the method of consumption or application. Some people report dry mouth, dizziness or paranoia when using cannabis. While many use cannabis to combat anxiety, it may create anxiety in others. Responsible dosing can help you avoid unpleasant experiences with cannabis.
 DRIVING & MACHINERY cannabis can slow your reaction time. Under M.G.L. c90, §24 it is illegal to drive or operate machinery under the influence of marijuana. When driving, keep your cannabis in a secure area of your vehicle, out of reach of the driver and passengers.
 FOOD. Do not consume cannabis infused products (edibles) on an empty stomach. We recommend eating a full meal before consuming cannabis infused products as it helps lower the intensity of effects. The undesirable effect will subside with time.
 LIMITS. You may purchase up to 2 ounces of cannabis flower or up to 10 grams of cannabis concentrate per day. Possessing more than the legal limit (2 oz. of Flower or each flower equivalency) outside of your place of residence may be penalized up to 6 months imprisonment or a $500 fine.
 PENALTIES. For information regarding penalties for possession or distribution of marijuana in violation of Massachusetts law please refer to M.G.L. c94G, §13 . Selling cannabis to others is illegal and a first offense (under 50 lbs.) can be punishable up to 2 years of imprisonment or a $5,000 fine.
 PREGNANCY certain health risks may be associated with consumption of cannabis while pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant.
 STATE BORDER. Stay in Massachusetts and do not cross state lines with cannabis products.
 STORAGE . Store cannabis securely, away from children and pets. Keep cannabis in the original child-proof packaging and away from other food items. To keep cannabis fresh, store in dark, dry and cool place.
 TOO MUCH OR TOO STRONG? Anxiety and paranoia may accompany accidental overdose. It is best to stay calm and remain in a comfortable and safe place.
 TOLERANCE, DEPENDENCE AND WITHDRAWAL . Although it is generally accepted that cannabis is not a physically addictive substance, a psychological dependence is possible with excessive usage of any substance. Please consume cannabis and cannabis products at your now risk. If you or someone you know is experiencing symptoms of substance abuse, consider talking to someone, your physician our counselor, about the drug use.
 
 Some examples of symptoms and signs of substance abuse are: 
 Neglecting responsibilities at school, work, or home because of drug use.
 Using drugs under dangerous conditions or taking risks while high.
 Built up a drug tolerance.
 Taking drugs to avoid or relieve withdrawal symptoms. Symptoms may include nausea, sweating, shakiness, and extreme anxiety.
 Causing problems in relationships.
 Abandoning previously enjoyed activities.
 Continuing using drugs, despite knowing it is hurting you.
 Losing control over drug use, may want to stop using, but feel powerless.
 Experiencing legal trouble, such as arrests for disorderly conduct, driving under the influence, or stealing to support a drug habit.
 
 If you or someone you know is exhibiting signs or symptoms of substance abuse please contact the Massachusetts substance abuse helpline at (800) 327-5050 for further assistance 
 
 
 DO’s 
 DO take your cannabis products directly from the dispensary to a private residence.
 DO keep your cannabis sealed and out of reach while in your motor vehicle. Cannabis cannot be transported once opened.
 DO store cannabis in a safe place away from direct sunlight and out of reach of any children or pets.
 DO consult your physician if you have any medical conditions before using cannabis.
 DON’Ts 
 Do NOT consume cannabis in public.
 Do NOT drive or operate heavy machinery while under the influence of cannabis.
 Do NOT consume cannabis with alcohol. Cannabis may increase the intensity of intoxication.
 Do NOT consume cannabis on National Seashore and bike trail.
 Do NOT travel out of the state of Massachusetts with your cannabis.
 Do NOT engage in the diversion of any marijuana products.
 
 How Much Weed Can I Buy at a Time? 
2 ounces of flower or 10 grams of concentrate. Up to 1000mg of edibles at a time, which can be up to 200 milligrams of THC. Please visit our Understanding the Daily Purchase Limit in MA page to calculate.
 
 How Much Am I Allowed to Possess? 
You’re allowed to hold up to ten ounces of marijuana in your home. If you’re on the street, the 2 ounce or 10 gram rule still applies. You also can’t go out in public, or drive around in your vehicle, with an open container of weed. This will earn you a fine of $500, so respect the law and keep it sealed up

Home / Lifecycle of a Cannabis Seed 
 

 Shop Cannabis Flower or Seeds for sale in Wellfleet, MA 

 Lifecycle of a Cannabis Seed

 This timeline is provided for educational purposes only and is intended to offer a general overview of the cannabis cultivation process from seed to harvest. Please note that results may vary depending on numerous factors, including strain genetics, growing environment, and cultivation methods. This information is not guaranteed to produce specific outcomes and should not be considered professional advice. Always follow local laws and best practices when cultivating cannabis.

 

 
 1-7 Days

 1. Germination Stage
 The cannabis lifecycle begins when a viable seed is exposed to moisture, warmth, and darkness. The seed absorbs water through its hard outer shell, activating internal enzymes and hormones. A white taproot (radicle) emerges as the seed cracks open, anchoring the future plant and beginning nutrient uptake.

Key Conditions:

• Temperature: 70–85°F (21–29°C)

• Humidity: 70–90%

• Darkness or low light

• Moist, not soaked, growing medium (paper towels, peat plugs, or soil)

Goal:

A strong taproot and first signs of life—ready for transplant into soil or a hydroponic medium.

 

 

 1-7 Days

 
 2-3 weeks

 2. Seedling Stage
 After germination, the seedling emerges above soil. The first cotyledon leaves (small, round seed leaves) appear, followed by the first true serrated cannabis leaves. This young plant is very delicate and needs proper conditions to develop a strong root system and stem.

Key Conditions:

• Light: 18–24 hours per day (low-intensity grow lights)

• Temperature: 68–77°F (20–25°C)

• Humidity: 65–70%

• Minimal nutrients (overfeeding can damage seedlings)

Goal:

Grow a sturdy, healthy base with at least 4–5 sets of true leaves before moving to vegetative growth.

 

 

 2-3 weeks

 
 3-8 weeks or longer

 3. Vegetative Stage
 This is the main growth phase. The plant rapidly develops branches, stems, and fan leaves, building energy through photosynthesis. Roots expand aggressively, and the plant can be trained (via topping, LST, etc.) to encourage bushier growth and increase future yields.

Key Conditions:

• Light: 18 hours on / 6 hours off

• Temperature: 70–85°F (21–29°C)

• Humidity: 40–70%

• Nutrients: High nitrogen (N) feed for structural growth

Goal:

Produce a robust, healthy plant with strong stems and multiple bud sites ready for flowering.

 

 

 3-8 weeks or longer

 
 1-2 weeks

 4. Pre-Flowering / Sexing Stage
 When transitioning from vegetative to flowering (typically by changing the light cycle), the plant shows signs of sex.

• Females show pistils (white hairs at nodes)

• Males form pollen sacs (round balls)

If growing from regular seeds, this is the time to identify and remove males (unless breeding). Feminized seeds skip this guessing game.

Key Conditions:

• Same as late vegetative stage

• Begin adjusting nutrient mix (lower nitrogen, more phosphorus)

Goal:

Identify plant sex and prepare females for full flowering.

 

 

 1-2 weeks

 
 6-12 weeks (Strain Dependent)

 5. Flowering Stage
 Once exposed to 12 hours of darkness, cannabis begins to flower. Female plants grow buds, which are clusters of calyxes covered in trichomes (resin glands with cannabinoids and terpenes). Buds thicken and ripen over time, developing their signature aroma, flavor, and potency.

Key Conditions:

• Light: 12 hours on / 12 off (strict)

• Temperature: 65–80°F (18–26°C)

• Humidity: 40–50% (lowering toward end to prevent mold)

• Nutrients: Lower nitrogen, higher phosphorus (P) and potassium (K)

Goal:

Grow dense, resinous, cannabinoid-rich buds for harvest.

 

 

 6-12 weeks (Strain Dependent)

 
 Timing depends on Strain

 6. Harvest Stage
 Once trichomes shift from clear to cloudy/amber, and pistils darken and curl, the plant is ready for harvest. Timing affects potency:

• Cloudy trichomes = peak THC

• Amber trichomes = more CBN (relaxing, sedative effect)

Key Steps:

• Flush plant with water (no nutrients) for 7–14 days pre-harvest

• Cut plant at the base or trim individual branches

• Handle gently to preserve trichomes

Goal:

Harvest at optimal ripeness for desired effects and potency.

 

 

 Timing depends on Strain

 
 2-6 weeks

 7. Drying & Curing
 Post-harvest, buds must be dried slowly to remove moisture without damaging cannabinoids. Then, curing in airtight containers allows flavors and potency to develop fully, reduces harshness, and preserves freshness.

Key Conditions (Drying):

• Temp: 60–70°F (16–21°C)

• Humidity: 50–60%

• Time: 7–14 days, in dark space with airflow

Key Conditions (Curing):

• Use glass jars, “burped” daily to release gases

• Continue for at least 2–4 weeks (up to 6+ weeks for premium results)

Goal:

Smooth, flavorful, potent buds with long shelf life and full terpene profile.

 

 

 2-6 weeks

 The full lifecycle of a cannabis seed from germination to harvest and curing takes approximately 3.5 to 6+ months , depending on the strain, growing conditions, and desired quality.
 
 Here’s a breakdown of how long each stage takes : 
 
 Stage 
 Timeframe 
 
 Germination
 1–7 days
 
 Seedling
 2–3 weeks
 
 Vegetative
 3–8 weeks (longer if desired)
 
 Pre-flowering/Sexing
 1–2 weeks
 
 Flowering
 6–12 weeks (strain dependent)
 
 Harvest
 1–3 days (includes trimming)
 
 Drying & Curing
 2–6 weeks (curing can go longer)
 
 
Typical Total Duration: 
 Fast grow (auto-flowering strains) : ~12–14 weeks (3–3.5 months) 

 Photoperiod grow (indoor/outdoor) : ~16–24 weeks (4–6 months+)

 Massachusetts Cannabis Purchase Limit Increased to 2 Ounces: What You Need to Know
 If you’ve been searching for information about the Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit , you’re not alone. One of the biggest changes to Massachusetts cannabis laws in recent years is the increase in the recreational cannabis purchase limit for adults 21 and older.
 
 Whether you’re a Massachusetts resident or visiting Cape Cod, understanding the Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit can help you shop confidently, stay compliant with state law, and better plan your visit to a licensed dispensary.
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis , we’re committed to providing accurate cannabis education and helping our customers stay informed about the latest cannabis laws and regulations.
 
 
 
 What Is the Massachusetts Cannabis Purchase Limit?
 As of April 20, 2026, the Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit for adult-use (recreational) consumers has increased from one ounce to two ounces of cannabis flower or its equivalent per day .
 
 The updated law was enacted through An Act Modernizing the Commonwealth’s Cannabis Laws (H.5350) and signed by Governor Maura Healey. The change is intended to modernize Massachusetts cannabis regulations while providing greater flexibility for adult consumers.
 
 For adults 21 years of age and older , the current Massachusetts recreational cannabis purchase limits include:
 
 Up to 2 ounces of cannabis flower 
 Up to 56 pre-roll joints , assuming each joint contains roughly 1 gram of flower .
 Up to 10 grams of active THC in cannabis concentrates 
 Up to 20 x 0.5g cartridges or 10 x 1g cartridges/disposables .
 Up to 1,000mg of THC in edible cannabis products 
 Up to 10,000mg of THC in Tinctures / Syrups 
 
 Topicals = NO LIMIT
 CBD = NO LIMIT
 Seeds = NO LIMIT
 
 These limits apply to purchases made from licensed adult-use (recreational) cannabis retailers in Massachusetts. Visit our Understanding the MA Daily Limit page for more information and calculator.
 
 
 
 Why Did the Massachusetts Cannabis Purchase Limit Change?
 The previous one ounce purchase limit had been in place since adult-use cannabis sales began in Massachusetts.
 
 As the regulated cannabis market has grown and matured, lawmakers recognized that many consumers wanted the convenience of purchasing larger quantities during a single visit instead of making multiple trips.
 
 The updated Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit provides greater flexibility while maintaining safeguards for responsible adult use.
 
 
 
 What Counts Toward the Massachusetts Cannabis Purchase Limit?
 Many customers wonder how different cannabis products count toward the daily purchase limit.
 
 The Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit applies to the combined total of cannabis products purchased during a single day.
 
 Popular product categories include:
 
 Flower
 Cannabis flower remains the most popular product purchased by recreational consumers. Flower is measured by weight and counts toward the two ounce daily purchase limit.
 
 
 Pre-Rolls
 Pre-rolls are simply ready to enjoy cannabis flower and also count toward your daily flower purchase limit.
 
 
 Edibles
 Cannabis infused gummies, chocolates, beverages , and other edible products count toward the daily limit based on their THC content.
 
 
 Concentrates
 Concentrates include products such as:
 Live Resin
 Live Rosin
 Wax
 Badder
 Shatter
 
 These products are subject to the state’s concentrate purchase limits because of their higher cannabinoid potency.
 
 
 Tinctures
 Cannabis tinctures provide a smoke free alternative and count toward your daily purchase limit based on their THC content.
 
 
 Vape Products
 Disposable vape products and vape cartridges are also included when calculating the legal purchase limit.
 
 
 What Has Not Changed?
 Although the Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit has increased, several important cannabis laws remain unchanged.
 
 Adults must still:
 
 Be at least 21 years old to purchase recreational cannabis.
 Present a VALID government issued photo identification.
 Consume cannabis only where permitted by law.
 Never drive while impaired by cannabis.
 Never transport cannabis across state lines, even into another legal cannabis state.
 
 Massachusetts law also continues to allow adults to possess up to 10 ounces of cannabis at home , with any amount over two ounces stored in a locked or secured container.
 
 
 What This Means for Cape Cod Visitors
 Every year, thousands of visitors travel to Cape Cod to enjoy the beaches, restaurants, outdoor recreation, and local attractions .
 
 For vacationers, the updated Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit for adult-use (recreational) means greater convenience. Instead of making multiple trips during a weeklong stay, eligible adults may be able to purchase everything they need during a single visit while remaining within Massachusetts law.
 
 If you’re searching for a dispensary near me while visiting Cape Cod, understanding the current purchase limits can help make your shopping experience easier and more enjoyable.

 What is the Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit?
 Adults 21 and older may purchase up to 2 ounces of cannabis flower or its legal equivalent from licensed recreational cannabis retailers in Massachusetts.
 
 Does the purchase limit apply to all cannabis products?
 Yes. Flower, pre rolls, edibles, concentrates, tinctures, vape products, and other cannabis products all count toward the legal daily purchase limit based on Massachusetts regulations.
 
 Can tourists buy cannabis in Massachusetts?
 Yes. Adults 21 and older with a VALID government issued photo ID may legally purchase recreational cannabis from licensed Massachusetts dispensaries.
 
 Can I take cannabis home to another state?
 No. Transporting cannabis across state lines remains illegal under federal law, even if cannabis is legal in both states.

 The updated Massachusetts cannabis purchase limit (recreational) gives adult consumers more flexibility while continuing to support responsible cannabis use throughout the Commonwealth.  July 22, 2026 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis News / Massachusetts Cannabis Repeal: What Every Voter Should Know 
 

 Massachusetts Cannabis Repeal: What Voters Need to Know Before the November 3, 2026 Election
 
 
 On Tuesday, November 3, 2026 , Massachusetts voters will decide the future of recreational cannabis in the Commonwealth.
 
 
 https://capecodcannabis.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/stop-the-repeal-All_Voting_v11_MC.mp4 

 
 
 
 
 
 A statewide ballot question seeks to repeal Massachusetts’ regulated adult use cannabis program. If approved, the measure would eliminate legal recreational cannabis sales across the state while leaving the medical cannabis program in place. The campaign opposing the repeal, Stop the Repeal , encourages voters to learn about the proposal and its potential impacts before Election Day.
 
 Whether you’re a Massachusetts resident, a Cape Cod local, or one of the millions of visitors who enjoy responsibly purchasing cannabis while vacationing on the Cape, understanding what’s at stake is important.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 What Is Question 8 on the November 3, 2026 Massachusetts Ballot?
 Question 8 asks Massachusetts voters whether to repeal the Commonwealth’s regulated adult use cannabis program. If approved, recreational cannabis sales would no longer be legal in Massachusetts, while the state’s medical cannabis program would remain in place.
 
 The proposal would reverse the voter-approved legalization of recreational cannabis that Massachusetts residents adopted in 2016. Supporters of the Stop the Repeal campaign encourage voters to reject Question 8, arguing that maintaining a regulated cannabis market protects consumers, supports local businesses, preserves jobs, and continues to generate important tax revenue for Massachusetts communities.
 
 As Election Day approaches, understanding what Question 8 would change is an important step in making an informed decision. Whether you are a Massachusetts resident or one of the many visitors who enjoy Cape Cod each year, staying informed about this statewide ballot question will help you understand how the outcome could affect the future of legal recreational cannabis throughout the Commonwealth.
 
 Quick Facts About Massachusetts Ballot Question 8 and Massachusetts Cannabis Repeal?
 
 Election Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
 Ballot Question: Question 8
 Proposal: Repeal Massachusetts’ regulated adult use recreational cannabis market
 Medical Cannabis: Would remain legal
 Who Can Vote: Registered Massachusetts voters 
 Learn More at Stop The Repeal MA: StopTheRepealMA.com 
 
 Note: On the November 3, 2026 Massachusetts ballot, the recreational cannabis repeal appears as Question 8 . If passed, Question 8 would repeal the Commonwealth’s regulated adult use cannabis program while leaving the medical cannabis program in place.
 
 IF this initiative passes it will have catastrophic affects, directly and indirectly, across Massachusetts: 
 
 Job losses: Over 21,000 individual agents and industry workers face displacement as commercial cultivation, manufacturing, and retail operations unwind.
 Tax revenue loss: An estimated annual loss of nearly $300 million in state taxes plus $50 million in municipal local-option taxes, squeezing local and state budgets that fund public health and addiction services.
 Business closures: Roughly 400 active retail storefronts would be forced to permanently shut down or transition strictly to medical-only sales.
 
 A repeal via Question 8 on the November 2026 ballot carries severe direct and indirect secondary losses. Beyond the immediate destruction of jobs and state revenue, cascading economic, regulatory, and public health losses would impact communities and adjacent industries across the state. 
 
 
 
 What Is the Massachusetts Cannabis Repeal Ballot Question?
 The ballot initiative proposes repealing the Commonwealth’s legal recreational cannabis market that Massachusetts voters originally approved in 2016.
 
 According to the campaign materials, supporters of the Stop the Repeal effort believe repeal would affect far more than licensed cannabis businesses. They argue it could impact local economies, tax revenue, consumer access, and public safety by eliminating the state’s regulated adult use marketplace.
 
 
 https://capecodcannabis.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/stop-the-repeal-Public_Health_v06_MC.mp4 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 What Could the Massachusetts Cannabis Repeal Mean?
 If the ballot question passes, Massachusetts would no longer allow licensed recreational cannabis sales.
 
 According to the Stop the Repeal campaign, repeal could have several impacts, including:
 
 The end of licensed adult use cannabis dispensaries across Massachusetts.
 Reduced tax revenue that currently supports state and local programs.
 Challenges for locally owned businesses that have invested in the regulated marketplace.
 Criminal penalties returning for certain non medical cannabis sales.
 A shift away from the regulated system that includes testing, labeling, and product safety standards.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 ADDENDUM: IF this initiative passes it will have catastrophic affects, directly and indirectly, across Massachusetts: 
 
 Job losses: Over 21,000 individual agents and industry workers face displacement as commercial cultivation, manufacturing, and retail operations unwind.
 Tax revenue loss: An estimated annual loss of nearly $300 million in state taxes plus $50 million in municipal local-option taxes, squeezing local and state budgets that fund public health and addiction services.
 Business closures: Roughly 400 active retail storefronts would be forced to permanently shut down or transition strictly to medical-only sales.
 
 A repeal via Question 8 on the November 2026 ballot carries severe direct and indirect secondary losses. Beyond the immediate destruction of jobs and state revenue, cascading economic, regulatory, and public health losses would impact communities and adjacent industries across the state. 
 
 Direct Losses
 Social Equity Funding Gutted: The Massachusetts Cannabis Social Equity Trust Fund , which has disbursed $28.9 million in grants to historically disadvantaged entrepreneurs, would be completely defunded and eliminated. [5]
 Commercial Real Estate Crash: Hundreds of specialized cultivation facilities, manufacturing centers, and retail properties would suddenly become vacant, leading to mass lease defaults and a collapse in commercial property values.
 Loss of Ancillary Businesses: Direct closures would extend to ancillary B2B sectors, including cannabis-focused security firms, specialized legal/accounting practices, software platforms, and testing laboratories. [6]
 Destruction of Personal Property Rights: Legal home cultivation of up to six plants per adult—a right Massachusetts residents have utilized since 2016—would be completely banned. [5, 7]
 
 
 Indirect Losses
 Public Health and Safety Backslide: The elimination of a regulated marketplace means a complete loss of mandatory lab testing (for heavy metals, mold, and pesticides), accurate THC dosage labeling, and strict age verification at the point of sale. [3, 8]
 Resurgence of the Illicit Market: Consumer demand will not vanish; instead, billions of dollars in economic activity will shift back to unregulated, untaxed illicit street markets. [3, 9]
 Collapse of Tourism and Hospitality: Massachusetts will lose its competitive edge as a regional tourism hub for visitors from neighboring states, impacting hotels, restaurants, and local transport options that thrive on foot traffic near dispensaries.
 Municipal Infrastructure Deficits: Cities and towns would lose the funding mechanism for local-option tax infrastructure projects. Money currently used to pave roads, fund public schools, and finance community programming would vanish. [3, 10, 11]
 Increased Pharmaceutical Reliance: Public health advocates note that therapeutic users who do not hold a formal medical card may be forced back toward addictive pharmaceutical alternatives (like opioids or sedatives) due to the loss of retail access. [12]
 
 
 
 
 Cannabis Control Commission Recognizes 10 Years of Adult-Use Cannabis in MA 
 Massachusetts voters approved the creation of an adult-use cannabis industry by ballot measure in November 2016 , the first state east of the Mississippi River to do so and the first state to have an equity mandate . Since then , Massachusetts has built one of the largest legal cannabis markets in the country with a network of nearly 800 licensed businesses across the Commonwealth, each one a major contributor to the state’s economy. 
 
 Check out the Cannabis Control Commision’s new initiative featuring economic data and a video capturing the highlights of the industry over the last decade.
 
 
 
 
 Why Regulation Matters
 Massachusetts has spent nearly a decade building one of the country’s most highly regulated cannabis markets.
 
 Licensed dispensaries operate under strict state regulations that include:
 
 Laboratory testing
 Child resistant packaging
 Product labeling
 Age verification
 Seed to sale tracking
 Consumer education
 Product recalls when necessary
 
 These safeguards help consumers make informed purchasing decisions while supporting a transparent marketplace.
 
 
 
 Supporting Local Massachusetts Businesses
 Since legalization, hundreds of Massachusetts businesses have opened their doors, creating thousands of jobs while contributing significant tax revenue to communities throughout the Commonwealth.
 
 The Stop the Repeal campaign states that legal cannabis sales have generated nearly $2 billion in state and local revenue since legalization in 2016.
 
 Many of these businesses are locally owned and operated, employing Massachusetts residents and supporting other local businesses through purchasing, partnerships, and community involvement.
 
 Here on Cape Cod, recreational cannabis has become part of the region’s tourism economy, serving both residents and adult visitors while operating under Massachusetts law.
 
 
 
 Consumer Safety Remains a Priority
 One of the primary goals of cannabis legalization has been moving consumers toward a regulated marketplace.
 
 Licensed dispensaries offer products that are:
 
 Tested for potency
 Screened for contaminants
 Clearly labeled
 Sold only to adults 21 years of age or older
 Produced and tracked under state regulations
 
 The Stop the Repeal campaign argues that maintaining a regulated legal market continues to provide important consumer protections.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 How Can You Learn More?
 The Stop the Repeal campaign encourages Massachusetts residents to:
 
 Learn about the ballot question.
 Verify their voter registration .
 Vote on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 .
 Volunteer or support public education efforts.
 Share factual information with family and friends.
 
 For additional information, visit: StopTheRepealMA.com 
 
 
 
 
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Is medical cannabis affected?
 
 According to the campaign, the ballot question focuses on Massachusetts’ recreational (adult-use) cannabis program. Medical cannabis would remain legal if the repeal measure were approved.
 
 
 
 When is the election?
 
 Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026 .
 
 
 
 Where can I learn more?
 
 Visit the official campaign website: StopTheRepealMA.com 
 
 
 
 Final Thoughts
 Massachusetts voters will make an important decision this November regarding the future of recreational cannabis in the Commonwealth. Register to vote today! 
 
 Regardless of where you stand, understanding the ballot question, reviewing reliable information, and participating in the democratic process are important steps in making an informed decision.
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis , we remain committed to education , responsible cannabis use, and helping adults better understand Massachusetts cannabis laws and regulations.
 
 If you’d like to learn more about cannabis, responsible consumption, or the products available in Massachusetts, our knowledgeable team is always happy to help.
 
 
 Sources

 Massachusetts Medical Marijuana Card: Pros and Cons

 
 
 
 
 
 January 9, 2022 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / Massachusetts Medical Marijuana Card: Pros and Cons 
 

 Massachusetts Medical Marijuana Card: Pros and Cons
 If you live in Massachusetts and use cannabis, you may have asked yourself if it’s worth it to invest in a medical marijuana card. Let’s weigh the pros and cons.
 
 Pros: 
 No taxes on medical cannabis. You will save quite a bit of money by not paying the 17-20% tax on recreational products.
 Discounts and sales are more widely available in the medical market, whereas recreational dispensaries are not technically allowed to offer discounts.
 You can use your MA med card in a few other states, including Maine and Rhode Island. Maine offers extremely competitive pricing for med card holders.
 Medical patients are prioritized over recreational shoppers. You’ll typically find more product availability, shorter lines, and a more professional experience.
 You can find products with higher potency than the 5 mg limit that recreational users have on single servings of edibles.
 
 Cons: 
 A med card does cost a few hundred dollars per year in fees.
 You could potentially run into issues if you hold a medical card and also want to own a gun.
 You will need to keep up with renewing your certification with your healthcare provider, as well as registration with the program (annually) and your program ID card (every three years).
 Having your card will not grant you immunity from being fired if your employer does not allow you to use cannabis.
 Depending on where you live, there may not be as many medical dispensaries as there are recreational. Here on Outer Cape Cod, locals drive as far as an hour and a half to stock up at the nearest medical dispensary.
 
 Taylor Sieg – CCC Product Specialist
 
 *Disclaimer Cape Cod Cannabis is a Recreational Dispensary. WE DO NOT ACCEPT MEDICAL CARDS!

 My Favorite Cannabis Products for Sleeping in Massachusetts

 
 
 
 
 
 November 21, 2021 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / My Favorite Cannabis Products for Sleeping in Massachusetts 
 

 My Favorite Cannabis Products for Sleeping in Massachusetts
 Working in cannabis retail for the past two years, I’ve found that one of the most common reasons people are coming into the dispensary is to find sleep-inducing products. Some are looking for help falling asleep initially while others need help getting back to sleep in the middle of the night. Luckily, cannabis can be extremely effective for any insomnia-riddled users. For those shopping in the adult use Massachusetts market, I’ve compiled a list of the products that have benefited myself the most.
 
 
 
 
 Dream Drops tincture by Treeworks. Tinctures are great for those waking up in the middle of the night because of the fast onset. I’m a huge fan of Treeworks tinctures specifically for two reasons. The first reason is that they produce full spectrum tinctures with RSO. RSO has many medicinal benefits on top of making the product feel more potent. My second reason is that they do a good job of masking the sometimes unpleasant taste of cannabis oil without adding any sugar. If you can’t find the Treeworks brand near you, look for another indica tincture product.
 
 Manna Speed Tabs in the “sleep” formula by Freshly Baked. Manna Speed Tabs have a five minute onset, making them my most used product. The sleep formula is half THC and half CBN. CBN is an extremely relaxing cannabinoid that is used often for getting to bed. Because of this ratio, I don’t find myself getting high from this product but I do find it impossible to keep my eyes open which is the main goal for me. Simply let the tablet(s) dissolve under your tongue right before you brush your teeth, and you’ll be ready to go.
 
 Cranberry Pomegranate gummies by Coast. These gummies offer a 1:1:1 ratio of THC, CBD, and CBN. Again, that CBN is going to add an extra sleepy aspect to the product. These will have a longer onset than the two previously mentioned products, which is anywhere from one to two hours. One perk of having a long onset is long duration of effects, so this is an ideal product for those seeking effects six to eight hours long.
 
 Cannatini’s Cranberry Lime Mojito gummies by North East Alternatives. This product isn’t directly marketed for sleep, but it provides a heavy body high that can be very sedative. The onset and duration of effects will be the same as the previous gummies. I’d recommend this to users who enjoy feeling high as well as those who need assistance relaxing at the end of the day. Just like the RSO-infused tincture we discussed, you may find these to be more potent and medicinally beneficial than distillate-infused gummies.
 
 Honorable mention: Bedtime Betty’s by Betty’s Eddies. These get an honorable mention because I don’t use them myself, but they are sought out frequently by those who have issues sleeping. Bedtime Betty’s features a candy similar to a taffy, infused with THC and melatonin. If you respond well to melatonin, you may find that having it in combination with THC is even more efficient. Onset of one to two hours and the effects will last six to eight hours.

 Home / Cape Cod Lifestyle / Outer Cape Music Festival 2026 
 

 Outer Cape Music Festival 2026 Returns to Wellfleet Labor Day Weekend
 
 
 
 
 Looking for one of the best Labor Day Weekend events on Cape Cod ? The Outer Cape Music Festival returns to Wellfleet Pier on Saturday, September 5 and Sunday, September 6, 2026 , bringing two days of live music, local talent, food, and community together for a great cause.
 
 With performances from nationally recognized artists, rising regional bands, and local favorites, the festival has become one of the premier live music events on the Outer Cape. Even better, 100% of all festival profits benefit local charities (see list below) , making it a weekend that supports both great music and the Cape Cod community.
 
 
 
 Saturday, September 5 Features Electro Gix
 Saturday’s headliner, Electro Gix , delivers an energetic blend of classic rock, dance hits, pop favorites, and crowd-pleasing anthems that keep audiences on their feet. Known throughout New England for their high-energy performances, Electro Gix is a festival favorite that brings excitement from the first song to the encore.
 
 Sharing the stage throughout the day are an impressive lineup of talented regional musicians, including:
 
 40 Thieves and Friends 
 The Boston Naturals 
 Natalia Bonfini Band 
 Club 9 Ball 
 Matt Devlin 
 
 Together, these artists offer a mix of rock, blues, Americana, soul, and original music that showcases the incredible talent found throughout Cape Cod and New England.
 
 
 
 Sunday, September
 The Sunday lineup features an outstanding collection of Cape Cod musicians and regional favorites, including:
 
 Crooked Coast 
 Bar Maids 
 Kami Lyle and Friends featuring Joey and Johnny Spampinato, Barbara Blazedell, and Tim Utt 
 Watch Your Step 
 
 From reggae and rock to blues, Americana, and contemporary originals, Sunday’s lineup offers something for music lovers of every age.
 
 
 
 More Than Just Great Music
 Beyond the performances, the Outer Cape Music Festival offers a vibrant waterfront atmosphere where visitors can enjoy local food, refreshments, and the unique charm of historic Wellfleet Harbor.
 
 Whether you’re a Cape Cod local or visiting for Labor Day Weekend, the festival is an excellent opportunity to experience the region’s thriving music scene while supporting local nonprofit organizations.
 
 
 
 Make a Weekend of It in Wellfleet
 Labor Day Weekend is one of the best times to visit the Outer Cape. Before or after the festival, spend time exploring Wellfleet’s beautiful beaches, art galleries, local shops, restaurants, and scenic harbor.
 
 If you’re 21 or older , stop by Cape Cod Cannabis , conveniently located just minutes from Wellfleet Pier. Our knowledgeable team is happy to help you explore premium flower, pre-rolls, edibles, vape products, concentrates, tinctures, CBD products, and more before enjoying the weekend’s festivities. Please consume responsibly and always follow Massachusetts cannabis laws.
 
 
 
 Plan Your Labor Day Weekend
 The Outer Cape Music Festival 2026 promises an unforgettable weekend of live entertainment, community spirit, and charitable giving in one of Cape Cod’s most beautiful waterfront settings.
 
 Mark your calendar for September 5 & 6, 2026 , gather your friends and family, and experience one of the best live music festivals on Cape Cod .
 
 For tickets and additional festival information, visit outercapemusicfest.com .
 
 
 
 100% of festival profits are donated to charity.
 The 2026 beneficiaries are:
 
 Lower Cape Outreach Council – Provides emergency food, clothing, financial assistance, and long-term self-sufficiency programs for residents of the eight Lower Cape towns.
 The Eastham/Orleans Elks Veterans Fund – Supports veterans, active military members, and their families through programs focused on employment, housing, health care, education, and military family assistance.
 The Lily House (Wellfleet) – A nonprofit community home that provides compassionate hospice and end-of-life care for terminally ill residents and support for their families.
 Friends of the Eastham Council on Aging – The Way Home Fund – Helps fund senior center programs, fitness classes, meals, transportation, educational opportunities, and other services for older adults in the Eastham community.
 Outer Cape Music Scholarship – Provides local children with access to music education by helping cover the cost of instruments and music lessons for families in need.
 Boston Children’s Hospital – Supports pediatric care, medical research, and family-centered services. The festival organizers note this charity holds special personal significance to their family.
 Wellfleet Food Pantry – Helps combat food insecurity by providing groceries and essential food supplies to Wellfleet residents and families experiencing hardship.
 
 These local and regional organizations reflect the festival’s mission of supporting the Outer Cape community while celebrating live music. Attending the festival not only offers a weekend of entertainment but also helps fund programs that provide food assistance, veteran services, hospice care, senior programs, music education, and pediatric healthcare.
 
 
 Visit Cape Cod Cannabis Before the Festival
 
 As a proud sponsor of the 2026 Outer Cape Music Festival , Cape Cod Cannabis is excited to support one of the Outer Cape’s premier Labor Day Weekend events and the local organizations that benefit from it.
 
 Before heading to Wellfleet Pier, stop by Cape Cod Cannabis at 1446 US-6 in the South Wellfleet Shopping Center , conveniently located just minutes from the festival. Explore one of Cape Cod’s largest selections of premium flower, pre-rolls, edibles, vape products, concentrates, tinctures, CBD products, and accessories. Whether you’re visiting Cape Cod for the weekend or you’re a local attending the festival, our knowledgeable team is here to help you find the products that best fit your preferences.
 
 Please remember: Cannabis consumption is not permitted at the festival or in public places. Consume responsibly and always follow Massachusetts cannabis laws.
