 Privacy Policy

 Cape Cod Cannabis and its affiliates (the “Company”) is committed to maintaining robust privacy protections for its users. Our Privacy Policy (“Privacy Policy”) is designed to help you understand how we collect, use and safeguard the information you provide to us and to assist you in making informed decisions when using our Service.
 
 For purposes of this Agreement, “Site” refers to the Company’s website, which can be accessed here . “Service” refers to the Company’s services accessed via the Site, in which users can browse our information and services, view educational material, view products, make appointments and place orders for pick up. The terms “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to the Company. “You” refers to you, as a user of our Site or our Service.
 
 By accessing our Site or our Service, you accept our Privacy Policy and Terms of Use , and you consent to our collection, storage, use and disclosure of your Personal Information as described in this Privacy Policy.
 
 I. INFORMATION WE COLLECT 
 We collect “Non-Personal Information” and “Personal Information.” Non-Personal Information includes information that cannot be used to personally identify you, such as anonymous usage data, general demographic information we may collect, referring/exit pages and URLs, platform types, preferences you submit and preferences that are generated based on the data you submit and number of clicks. Personal Information includes your email, date of birth and contact information, which you submit to us through the registration process at the Site.
 
 1. Information collected via Technology
 To activate the Service you do not need to submit any Personal Information other than your date of birth. To use the Service thereafter, you do not need to submit further Personal Information, which may include: email, date of birth and contact information. However, in an effort to improve the quality of the Service, we track information provided to us by your browser or by our software application when you view or use the Service, such as the website you came from (known as the “referring URL”), the type of browser you use, the device from which you connected to the Service, the time and date of access, and other information that does not personally identify you. We track this information using cookies, or small text files which include an anonymous unique identifier. Cookies are sent to a user’s browser from our servers and are stored on the user’s computer hard drive. Sending a cookie to a user’s browser enables us to collect Non-Personal information about that user and keep a record of the user’s preferences when utilizing our services, both on an individual and aggregate basis. For example, the Company may use cookies to collect the following information: location.
 
 The Company may use both persistent and session cookies; persistent cookies remain on your computer after you close your session and until you delete them, while session cookies expire when you close your browser.
 
 2. Information you provide us by registering for an account
 In addition to the information provided automatically by your browser when you visit the Site, to become a subscriber to the Service you will need to create a personal profile. You can create a profile by registering with the Service and entering your email address, and creating a user name and a password. By registering, you are authorizing us to collect, store and use your email address in accordance with this Privacy Policy.
 
 3. Children’s Privacy
 The Site and the Service are not directed to anyone under the age of 21. The Site does not knowingly collect or solicit information from anyone under the age of 21, or allow anyone under the age of 21 to sign up for the Service. In the event that we learn that we have gathered personal information from anyone under the age of 21 without the consent of a parent or guardian, we will delete that information as soon as possible. If you believe we have collected such information, please contact us at info@capecodcannabis.com.
 
 II. HOW WE USE AND SHARE INFORMATION 
 Personal Information: 
 Except as otherwise stated in this Privacy Policy, we do not sell, trade, rent or otherwise share for marketing purposes your Personal Information with third parties without your consent. We do share Personal Information with vendors who are performing services for the Company, such as the servers for our email communications who are provided access to user’s email address for purposes of sending emails from us. Those vendors use your Personal Information only at our direction and in accordance with our Privacy Policy.
 
 In general, the Personal Information you provide to us is used to help us communicate with you. For example, we use Personal Information to contact users in response to questions, solicit feedback from users, provide technical support, and inform users about promotional offers.
 
 We may share Personal Information with outside parties if we have a good-faith belief that access, use, preservation or disclosure of the information is reasonably necessary to meet any applicable legal process or enforceable governmental request; to enforce applicable Terms of Service, including investigation of potential violations; address fraud, security or technical concerns; or to protect against harm to the rights, property, or safety of our users or the public as required or permitted by law.
 
 Non-Personal Information: 
 In general, we use Non-Personal Information to help us improve the Service and customize the user experience. We also aggregate Non-Personal Information in order to track trends and analyze use patterns on the Site. This Privacy Policy does not limit in any way our use or disclosure of Non-Personal Information and we reserve the right to use and disclose such Non-Personal Information to our partners, advertisers and other third parties at our discretion.
 
 In the event we undergo a business transaction such as a merger, acquisition by another company, or sale of all or a portion of our assets, your Personal Information may be among the assets transferred. You acknowledge and consent that such transfers may occur and are permitted by this Privacy Policy, and that any acquirer of our assets may continue to process your Personal Information as set forth in this Privacy Policy. If our information practices change at any time in the future, we will post the policy changes to the Site so that you may opt out of the new information practices. We suggest that you check the Site periodically if you are concerned about how your information is used.
 
 III. HOW WE PROTECT INFORMATION 
 We implement security measures designed to protect your information from unauthorized access. Your account is protected by your account password and we urge you to take steps to keep your personal information safe by not disclosing your password and by logging out of your account after each use. We further protect your information from potential security breaches by implementing certain technological security measures including encryption, firewalls and secure socket layer technology. However, these measures do not guarantee that your information will not be accessed, disclosed, altered or destroyed by breach of such firewalls and secure server software. By using our Service, you acknowledge that you understand and agree to assume these risks.
 
 IV. YOUR RIGHTS REGARDING THE USE OF YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION 
 You have the right at any time to prevent us from contacting you for marketing purposes. When we send a promotional communication to a user, the user can opt out of further promotional communications by following the unsubscribe instructions provided in each promotional e-mail. You can also indicate that you do not wish to receive marketing communications from us in the “Unsubscribe” section of the Site. Please note that notwithstanding the promotional preferences you indicate by either unsubscribing or opting out in the unsubscribe page of the Site, we may continue to send you administrative emails including, for example, periodic updates to our Privacy Policy.
 
 V. LINKS TO OTHER WEBSITES 
 As part of the Service, we may provide links to or compatibility with other websites or applications. However, we are not responsible for the privacy practices employed by those websites or the information or content they contain. This Privacy Policy applies solely to information collected by us through the Site and the Service. Therefore, this Privacy Policy does not apply to your use of a third party website accessed by selecting a link on our Site or via our Service. To the extent that you access or use the Service through or on another website or application, then the privacy policy of that other website or application will apply to your access or use of that site or application. We encourage our users to read the privacy statements of other websites before proceeding to use them.
 
 VI. CHANGES TO OUR PRIVACY POLICY 
 The Company reserves the right to change this policy and our Terms of Service at any time. We will notify you of significant changes to our Privacy Policy by sending a notice to the primary email address specified in your account or by placing a prominent notice on our site. Significant changes will go into effect 30 days following such notification. Non-material changes or clarifications will take effect immediately. You should periodically check the Site and this privacy page for updates.
 
 VII. CONTACT US 
 If you have any questions regarding this Privacy Policy or the practices of this Site, please use our contact us form.

Home / Receive Web & iOS Push Notifications 
 

 Receive Push Notifications from Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet, MA 

 
 Get instant updates for New Product Drops, Bundle Offers, and alerts delivered straight to your device from Cape Cod Cannabis — no matter where you are.
 
 
 What Are Web Push Notifications?
 Web Push Notifications are quick messages sent to your browser—even when you’re not on the site. No app needed and you can unsubscribe at any time. 
 
 
 How to Enable Notifications
 Visit our website in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge.
 Click Allow on the notification prompt.
 Manage notifications anytime in your browser settings (allow pop-ups, etc.) .
 Please clear your browser cache and refresh our site if you do not see our notification window (below). 
 Cannot subscribe while in Incognito or private browsing mode
 
 
 
 
 What Are iOS Push Notifications?
 iOS Push Notifications send alerts directly to your iPhone or iPad from apps or supported websites.
 
 
 How to Enable iOS Notifications
 Go to https://capecodcannabis.com on your iOS browser
 Add our website to your Home Screen and Save
 Open the CCC icon from the home screen (not the browser)
 Interact with our subscribe button “Save Preferences” to trigger the native permission prompt.
 
 
 
 
 Manage Your Notifications
 Customize or disable notifications anytime.
 Ensure device and browser settings allow alerts.
 Stay connected with real-time updates and offers.

 Recreational Benefits of Using Cannabis
 Cannabis can provide countless benefits to a wide variety of different people; benefits that don’t have to be just for medicinal purposes. Those who are just starting to experiment can often overlook all that this plant has to offer. I’ve compiled a list of potential effects that users have shared with me in the past that you too may find to be useful. Just remember that not everyone responds to cannabis in the same exact way. In fact, it’s not uncommon for people to experience differents highs when sharing the same joint. Seeking out specific effects from various strains will be trial-and-error so remember not to get discouraged if you don’t immediately find what you’re looking for. “One man’s trash is another man’s treasure” is extremely applicable to cannabis. Try keeping a log or diary of what works for you and what doesn’t so you don’t forget.
 
 Productivity. Look for a strain that gives you energizing effects and you may find yourself suddenly inspired to wash your dishes, do some laundry, or clean out the attic. Try: Haze, Durban Poison
 
 Creativity. Whether it’s painting, writing, or playing music, you could find that the creative juices start flowing after indulging in a toke or two. Try: Chemdawg, LSD
 
 Arousal. Cannabis can be beneficial for both men and women when it comes to getting in the mood and enhancing certain sensations. Some strains can have the complete opposite effect though so beware. Try: Strawberry Cough, Mimosa
 
 Socializing. While it’s common for new users to feel a bit of social anxiety when first experimenting, there are several strains out there that can actually make you feel more comfortable when hanging out with friends. Try: Girl Scout Cookies, ACDC
 
 Exercising. If you haven’t caught on by now, the idea that stoners are always couch-locked and lazy is a thing of the past. People are now using cannabis for motivation before they hit the gym or go on a hike. Try: Super Lemon Haze, Green Crack
 
 Studying. Yes, cannabis can even help people find the motivation to study as well as focus on what they’re working on. I got through many of my college classes with help from Mary Jane. Try: Tangie, Harlequin
 
 Unwinding. Probably one of the most common reasons for recreational users to get high is just simply relaxing at the end of the day and relieving the tension and stress from your body. Try: Zkittlez, Bubba Kush
 
 If you get the chance to stop in at Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet, I recommend checking out the effect-based wall where products are sorted by how they may make you feel.

 Bourne, Massachusetts, is a gateway town to Cape Cod, known for its scenic beauty, historical significance, and relaxed atmosphere. Located at the westernmost point of the Cape, Bourne is the first town visitors encounter when crossing the iconic Bourne and Sagamore Bridges, which span the Cape Cod Canal. The canal is a major feature of the town, offering a variety of outdoor activities such as biking, walking, fishing, and boat-watching along its picturesque paths.
 
 Bourne is home to several charming villages, each with its own unique character. These include Buzzards Bay, the town’s bustling hub; Monument Beach, known for its tranquil sandy shorelines; and Pocasset and Cataumet, which feature quiet residential areas and lovely coastal views. The town’s beaches, such as Scusset Beach and Monument Beach, provide opportunities for swimming, boating, and enjoying the scenic Cape Cod coastline.
 
 Bourne has a rich history that is reflected in its many historic sites and landmarks. The Aptucxet Trading Post Museum is one of the oldest sites in the region, dating back to the 1600s, offering insights into early colonial and Native American trade. The Cape Cod Canal Railroad Bridge, a unique vertical-lift bridge, is a striking landmark that highlights the town’s importance as a transportation hub.
 
 In addition to its natural and historical attractions, Bourne offers a range of recreational activities. The Cape Cod Canal, in particular, is a favorite for cyclists, joggers, and nature lovers, while the town’s golf courses, parks, and marinas provide ample opportunities for outdoor enjoyment.
 
 With its mix of coastal beauty, historic charm, and outdoor activities, Bourne serves as both an inviting gateway to Cape Cod and a peaceful destination in its own right. It’s a perfect place for those seeking a relaxed, scenic experience with easy access to both the mainland and the rest of the Cape.

 Where can I find weed near me on Cape Cod? 
 If you’re searching for weed near me on Cape Cod , Cape Cod Cannabis is an adult-use recreational dispensary located at 1446 US-6 in Wellfleet, Massachusetts , in the South Wellfleet area of the Outer Cape. We’re open daily and offer a wide selection of recreational cannabis products. Customers 21+ can shop in-store or order online for convenient pickup with valid ID.

 
 
 
 
 
 What is the legal age to purchase cannabis in Massachusetts? 
 We welcome anyone 21 years of age or older with a valid Government ID (e.g., Drivers License, Passport, etc.) to verify your age upon entry. Unfortunately, we cannot accept expired MA ID’s unless, when already renewed, you bring the expired MA ID with the actual MA RMV documentation for the renewal.
 
 Unfortunately, we cannot accept any out-of-state or International ID’s that are expired. 
 
 Note : We respect if you are wearing a mask when you enter but please know that, per regulations, we have to properly identify everyone who enters. You will be asked to momentarily remove (or lower) your mask for identification purposes. We thank you for your cooperation and understanding. 

 
 
 
 
 
 What should I expect when visiting a dispensary for the first time? 
 If it’s your first time visiting a dispensary in Massachusetts, the process is simple and welcoming. When you arrive, you’ll be asked to show a valid government-issued ID to confirm you are 21 or older. After check-in, you can browse the menu or speak with a knowledgeable staff member (often called a budtender) who can help you choose products based on your preferences and experience level.
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis, you’ll find a variety of options including flower , pre-rolls , edibles , vapes , tinctures , topicals , CBD and concentrates . Our budtenders are here to answer questions and make recommendations, whether you’re looking to relax, sleep better, or try cannabis for the first time. Once you’ve made your selection, you’ll proceed to checkout—we accept cash and debit payment options. We also have an on-site ATM for your convenience.
 
 Overall, expect a safe, regulated, and educational experience designed to help you feel comfortable and informed…and NOT rushed.
 
 We also offer an online assistant (bottom left side of the website) to ask questions and lead you in the right direction. Please give us a call at (774) 383-3133 if you have further questions.

 2026 Cape Cod Choice Awards: Best CBD Store Winner | Top 3 Best Cannabis Dispensary

 What are the operating hours for Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 We’re open 7 days a week. Please check our hours for the most up-to-date hours, including holiday schedules.

 
 
 
 
 
 What cannabis products do you carry? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Dispensary in Wellfleet offers the largest selection of quality flower , pre-rolls , seeds , edibles , vapes , concentrates , syrups / tinctures , CBD , topicals , pet drops and more at the BEST prices on Cape Cod…something for every preference and experience level.  Is there a limit to how much cannabis I can buy? 
 Yes. As of April 19, 2026 , Massachusetts law allows you to purchase up to 2 ounces of flower (Recreational) or its equivalent in other cannabis products per day.
 
 Click here to visit our “Understanding the Daily Purchase Limit in MA” page for more information and to calculate your daily purchase.
 
 Recreational = 56 grams (flower) a day is the legal MA limit, which can constitute: 
 
 • Flower : Up to 56 grams (2 ounces).
 • Edibles : A total of 10 00mg THC , which is roughly 10 packs of 20 servings , each serving containing 5mg of THC .
 • Concentrates : Up to 10 grams of cannabis concentrates, such as wax, shatter, or live resin (equivalent to 10 x 1g or 20 x 0.5g packages).
 • Tinctures : A total of 10000mg = approximately 10 x 1000mg bottles , depending on the product’s potency and total THC content.
 • Pre-roll Joints : 56 pre-roll joints , assuming each joint contains roughly 1 gram of flower .
 • Vape Cartridges : Up to 20 x 0.5g cartridges or 10 x 1g cartridges/disposables .
 
 CBD = No Limit 
 Topicals = No Limit 
 Accessories = No Limit 

 
 
 
 
 
 Are your cannabis products tested for safety and quality? 
 Yes. Cannabis products sold at Cape Cod Cannabis are required to meet Massachusetts testing and labeling requirements before being offered for retail sale.

 
 
 
 
 
 What payment methods are accepted? 
 We accept cash, debit cards and CanPay . A regular ATM is also located on-site for your convenience.
 
 Note : ATM and Debit transactions will incur a small third-party merchant fee. 

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you offer online ordering or pre-orders?

 Once you finalize your order, it will be filled within 15 minutes and you will be able to pick it up at the store. Changes to pre-orders can be made during checkout at the store.
 
 PLEASE double check your phone number when entering your pre-order. 
 
 We will not keep orders placed, past our store closing, the day of when the order was placed.

 
 
 
 
 
 What should I know about cannabis?

 Do you offer a Loyalty Program? 
 Yes! We do offer a FREE Loyalty VIP Program where you can accumulate points that will be generated automatically and tracked for you for redemption.
 
 NOTE : Per MA Cannabis Control Commission regulations, Loyalty Points CANNOT be used for cannabis products . 
 
 Currently, y ou CAN use your Loyalty Points toward Cape Cod Cannabis CBD, Accessories or Merch only. 
 
 As soon as the CCC ( Cannabis Control Commission ) will approve or will remove the limitations on the promotions, you will be able to use these points toward all Cape Cod Cannabis products. That way you will not miss out on any points you could have accumulated if there were no limitations to begin with. In the meantime, you will get access to the VIP program.

 Sign up for our free Loyalty VIP Program in-store and receive exclusive info on new product drops and pricing offers, events, and earn loyalty points with every purchase that you can redeem for Accessories, Apparel or CBD !

 Already a Loyalty VIP Member?

 * Important : Please tell your Product Specialist that you’d like to redeem your Loyalty VIP Points at the time of purchase.

 CLICK HERE TO VIEW FAQs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Where is Cape Cod Cannabis located? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Recreational Dispensary is located at 1446 US-6, Wellfleet, MA 02667 . We’re conveniently located along Route 6 in the South Wellfleet shopping plaza, designed like a rest stop, for easy entry and exit with plenty of free parking, includes a bakery, liquor store, and U.S. Post Office for your convenience. Click here for directions . 
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis is a licensed adult-use recreational dispensary serving residents and visitors alike in Barnstable , Bourne , Brewster , Chatham , Dennis , Eastham , Falmouth , Harwich , Hyannis , Mashpee , Orleans , Provincetown , Sandwich , Truro , Wellfleet , Yarmouth and beyond. 

 
 
 
 
 
 Where can I find weed near me on Cape Cod? 
 If you’re searching for weed near me on Cape Cod , Cape Cod Cannabis is an adult-use recreational dispensary located at 1446 US-6 in Wellfleet, Massachusetts , in the South Wellfleet area of the Outer Cape. We’re open daily and offer a wide selection of recreational cannabis products. Customers 21+ can shop in-store or order online for convenient pickup with valid ID.

 
 
 
 
 
 What is the legal age to purchase cannabis in Massachusetts? 
 We welcome anyone 21 years of age or older with a valid Government ID (e.g., Drivers License, Passport, etc.) to verify your age upon entry. Unfortunately, we cannot accept expired MA ID’s unless, when already renewed, you bring the expired MA ID with the actual MA RMV documentation for the renewal.
 
 Unfortunately, we cannot accept any out-of-state or International ID’s that are expired. 
 
 Note : We respect if you are wearing a mask when you enter but please know that, per regulations, we have to properly identify everyone who enters. You will be asked to momentarily remove (or lower) your mask for identification purposes. We thank you for your cooperation and understanding. 

 
 
 
 
 
 What should I expect when visiting a dispensary for the first time? 
 If it’s your first time visiting a dispensary in Massachusetts, the process is simple and welcoming. When you arrive, you’ll be asked to show a valid government-issued ID to confirm you are 21 or older. After check-in, you can browse the menu or speak with a knowledgeable staff member (often called a budtender) who can help you choose products based on your preferences and experience level.
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis, you’ll find a variety of options including flower , pre-rolls , edibles , vapes , tinctures , topicals , CBD and concentrates . Our budtenders are here to answer questions and make recommendations, whether you’re looking to relax, sleep better, or try cannabis for the first time. Once you’ve made your selection, you’ll proceed to checkout—we accept cash and debit payment options. We also have an on-site ATM for your convenience.
 
 Overall, expect a safe, regulated, and educational experience designed to help you feel comfortable and informed…and NOT rushed.
 
 We also offer an online assistant (bottom left side of the website) to ask questions and lead you in the right direction. Please give us a call at (774) 383-3133 if you have further questions.

 
 
 
 
 
 What do customers say about Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 
 2026 Cape Cod Choice Awards: Best CBD Store Winner | Top 3 Best Cannabis Dispensary 
 Customers frequently mention our knowledgeable and friendly team, wide cannabis selection, personalized service, welcoming atmosphere, convenient Route 6 location, and overall dispensary experience. Read our recent customer reviews to see feedback directly from customers.

 
 
 
 
 
 Can I leave a review for Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 Yes. Visit our Leave Your Review page to share your experience on Google or Yelp.

 
 
 
 
 
 What are the operating hours for Cape Cod Cannabis? 
 We’re open 7 days a week. Please check our hours for the most up-to-date hours, including holiday schedules.

 
 
 
 
 
 What cannabis products do you carry? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Dispensary in Wellfleet offers the largest selection of quality flower , pre-rolls , seeds , edibles , vapes , concentrates , syrups / tinctures , CBD , topicals , pet drops and more at the BEST prices on Cape Cod…something for every preference and experience level. Always worth the trip! 

 
 
 
 
 
 Is there a limit to how much cannabis I can buy? 
 Yes. As of April 19, 2026 , Massachusetts law allows you to purchase up to 2 ounces of flower (Recreational) or its equivalent in other cannabis products per day.
 
 Click here to visit our “Understanding the Daily Purchase Limit in MA” page for more information and to calculate your daily purchase.
 
 Recreational = 56 grams (flower) a day is the legal MA limit, which can constitute: 
 
 • Flower : Up to 56 grams (2 ounces).
 • Edibles : A total of 10 00mg THC , which is roughly 10 packs of 20 servings , each serving containing 5mg of THC .
 • Concentrates : Up to 10 grams of cannabis concentrates, such as wax, shatter, or live resin (equivalent to 10 x 1g or 20 x 0.5g packages).
 • Tinctures : A total of 10000mg = approximately 10 x 1000mg bottles , depending on the product’s potency and total THC content.
 • Pre-roll Joints : 56 pre-roll joints , assuming each joint contains roughly 1 gram of flower .
 • Vape Cartridges : Up to 20 x 0.5g cartridges or 10 x 1g cartridges/disposables .
 
 CBD = No Limit 
 Topicals = No Limit 
 Accessories = No Limit 

 
 
 
 
 
 Are your cannabis products tested for safety and quality? 
 Yes. Cannabis products sold at Cape Cod Cannabis are required to meet Massachusetts testing and labeling requirements before being offered for retail sale.

 
 
 
 
 
 What payment methods are accepted? 
 We accept cash, debit cards and CanPay . A regular ATM is also located on-site for your convenience.
 
 Note : ATM and Debit transactions will incur a small third-party merchant fee. 

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you offer online ordering or pre-orders? 
 Yes! Browse our full menu online or our Daily Offers page and place a pre-order for quick and easy pickup in-store.
 
 Once you finalize your order, it will be filled within 15 minutes and you will be able to pick it up at the store. Changes to pre-orders can be made during checkout at the store.
 
 PLEASE double check your phone number when entering your pre-order. 
 
 We will not keep orders placed, past our store closing, the day of when the order was placed.

 
 
 
 
 
 What should I know about cannabis? 
 For a quick overview of the different types of cannabis products, terpenes, cannabinoids, strains and more please visit Intro to Cannabis 101 .

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you offer a Loyalty Program? 
 Yes! We do offer a FREE Loyalty VIP Program where you can accumulate points that will be generated automatically and tracked for you for redemption.
 
 NOTE : Per MA Cannabis Control Commission regulations, Loyalty Points CANNOT be used for cannabis products . 
 
 Currently, y ou CAN use your Loyalty Points toward Cape Cod Cannabis CBD, Accessories or Merch only. 
 
 As soon as the CCC ( Cannabis Control Commission ) will approve or will remove the limitations on the promotions, you will be able to use these points toward all Cape Cod Cannabis products. That way you will not miss out on any points you could have accumulated if there were no limitations to begin with. In the meantime, you will get access to the VIP program.
 
 Not a Loyalty Program VIP member? JOIN FOR FREE IN-STORE TODAY! 
 
 Already a Loyalty Program VIP member? Click here to Shop your Loyalty VIP Points. 

 
 
 
 
 
 What is your Return Policy? 
 Cape Cod Cannabis is committed to customer satisfaction when it comes to the products we sell.
 
 RETURN POLICY 
 Please visit our Return Policy page for more information.
 
 CONTACT US 
 If you have any questions regarding our Return Policy please contact us or call (774) 383-3133.

 
 
 
 
 
 What is your Privacy Policy? 
 PRIVACY POLICY 
 Please visit our Privacy Policy page for more information.
 
 CONTACT US 
 If you have any questions regarding this Privacy Policy please contact us or call us at (774) 383-3133.

 
 
 
 
 
 Do you ship your Apparel? 
 Yes! Our apparel, hats, beanies, sweatshirts, joggers and more can be shipped to you (within the United States only) via USPS Priority. Please visit our online store Blue Tail Apparel & Merch @ www.BlueTail.cc for convenient, safe and easy shopping and we will ship your order to you!
 
 Of course, you can always pre-order Cape Cod Cannabis apparel , accessories and merch for local pickup.
 
 * Please note : Loyalty Points do not apply for purchases on BlueTail.cc at this time. 
 
 In-store or pre-order (non-cannabis) purchases on CapeCodCannabis.com are applicable using your Loyalty Points.

 Stepping into a Dispensary for the First Time

 
 
 
 
 
 November 7, 2021 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / Stepping into a Dispensary for the First Time 
 

 Stepping into a Dispensary for the First Time
 A first time dispensary visit can be a little overwhelming or intimidating for new users. Depending on the state and dispensary, there will likely be security officers on site. You’ll be asked for your valid government ID at least once or twice. Keep in mind that this isn’t to annoy you, but to keep a track on everyone’s purchasing limit and ensure nobody is checked out under the wrong name. You will typically wait in a lobby until a budtender becomes available. Their role is to guide you along the way as you pick products out, answering any questions and making product recommendations.
 
 Once you are brought to the sales counter, you’ll be shown a menu with a long list of items. Having an idea of the sort of cannabis products you’d like to use will give your budtender some guidance during the consultation. Common options available at most dispensaries include flower, edibles, tinctures, concentrates, and topicals. If you plan on purchasing buds of cannabis flower to smoke, the most traditional way of using cannabis, then you will want to familiarize yourself with the following terms:
 
 Gram = Typically the smallest quantity you can purchase of whole buds 

 Eighth = 3.5 grams, and the most common quantity sold 

 Quarter = 7 grams 

 Half = 14 grams 

 Ounce = 28 grams 

 Pre-rolls = Flower already rolled into a joint or blunt for your convenience 
 
 You should also consider the effects you’d like to feel. Cannabis products that provide you with cerebral effects which are mood-enhancing, euphoric, and energizing will be referred to as sativa. Sativa effects tend to be the most social and can be great for a daytime high, depending on the person. On the opposite end of the spectrum are indica products. These will provide a body high that is relaxing and pain-relieving. Many people use indicas in the evening to unwind, but those who suffer from chronic pain may be more inclined to indulge all day long. Hybrid products will have a combination of effects. Some may lean more indica or sativa, but the idea is that the effects will be a bit more balanced. Not overly relaxing, not overly euphoric.
 
 Now your last step after picking out your products is paying. I bring this up because payment methods offered can be pretty scarce due to cannabis still being federally illegal. Most banks comply with federal law and regulations which means it’s common to not be able to use debit or credit cards at pot shops, though there are a small few that do. Some dispensaries have cashless ATMs that allow you to swipe a debit card at checkout instead of taking out the cash at an ATM, essentially saving you an extra step. You may even be able to use a money transfer service, such as CanPay, which allows you to transfer money straight from your bank account to the business. If you’re unsure of what to expect then bring cash just in case.

Cape Cod Cannabis Dispensary in Wellfleet
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis, Wellfleet’s first dispensary, our mission is to cultivate a vibrant and sustainable cannabis community, rooted in the spirit of the Cape, where the beauty of the region is celebrated through responsible and innovative cannabis practices. We are committed to providing our customers with the highest quality cannabis products while promoting education, accessibility, and well-being.
 
 We believe in the power of cannabis to enhance lives, alleviate pain, and foster a sense of wellness. Our dedicated team is passionate about delivering safe and reliable cannabis products that meet the diverse needs of our community. We are driven by a commitment to quality, transparency, and sustainability in all aspects of our operations.
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Dispensary in Wellfleet offers the largest selection of quality products and the best prices on Cape Cod. Our product assortment includes flower , pre-rolls , edibles , beverages , vaporizers , tinctures , concentrates , CBD products , topicals , seeds , smoking accessories and branded apparel (need our Apparel shipped to you? Visit www.BlueTail.cc to order) .
 
 Our knowledgeable and friendly staff will ensure that you have a pleasant and informed shopping experience and our security staff ensure convenient and safe parking in our designated spaces during the store’s operating hours.
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Dispensary in Wellfleet…it’s worth the trip!

Hybrid Products

 Summer 2025 Season Kick‑Off: 4th of July 2025 – Cape Cod Cannabis style in Wellfleet! 
 Summer’s almost here—and so is the Independence Day weekend you’ve been waiting for! Whether you’re a Cape Cod local or soaking up the salty breeze as a visitor, Cape Cod Cannabis Recreational Dispensary in South Wellfleet is your go-to cannabis stop to gear up for a festive, memorable 4th.
 
 
 
 
 
 What’s Happening on Cape Cod for 4th of July 2025? 
 Wellfleet Hometown Parade 
 Classic cars roll down Holbrook Avenue at 9:30 AM sharp—followed by the main parade with floats, and local flair at 10 AM along Main Street.

 Fireworks in the Outer Cape 
 Catch majestic evening displays in Provincetown Harbor or nearby towns—fireworks abound.

 Baseball Under the Lights 
 Cap your day with Cape Cod Baseball League games across the region—summer classics with family vibes.

 Cape Cod Cannabis Recreational Dispensary 
 Open daily for adults 21+ offering the largest selection of quality products at the best prices on Cape Cod.

 
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis: Your Holiday Cannabis HQ 
 Located in the Route 6 shopping plaza in South Wellfleet, we’re open daily and ready to help you elevate your holiday weekend. From 8 AM to 9 PM (Fri-Sat) and 8 AM to 8 PM on (Sun-Thurs), we’re here early and late to support all your celebration needs. Shop our full menu .
 
 Stock up on fan-favorite flower , pre-rolls , refreshing edibles , vaporizers , concentrates , tinctures , accessories , and our exclusive summer merch . Plus, join our Loyalty VIP Program and Blazing Bargains & Bundles you won’t want to miss.
 
 
 Plan Your Day Cape Cod Style 
 Morning – Parade, family fun, and maybe a scenic bike ride along the Cape Cod Rail Trail.

 Afternoon – Chill at Marconi Beach with seal sightings and salty air —or catch a baseball game.

 Any time of the day – Easy stop at Cape Cod Cannabis for extras like flower , pre-rolls , edibles , vapes , or cool accessories. Check out our Bundles & Blazing Bargains too!

 Night – Head out to enjoy fireworks reflecting over the harbor—pure Independence Day magic.

 Have fun, be safe – And, as always, celebrate responsibly.
 
 
 
 
 
 Why Cape Cod Cannabis is The Best Recreational Dispensary on Cape Cod… 
 Local and Visitor Friendly with Cool Vibes – Welcoming and knowledgable staff serving Cape Cod and tourists alike.

 The Largest Selection of Quality Products at the Best Prices on Cape Cod – Flower , pre-rolls , edibles , vapes , concentrates , CBD , tinctures —you name it.

 Convenience – Online ordering , easy parking, Route 6 access—no stress, just chill. It’s worth the trip! 

 Summer Deals & Blazing Bargains – Bundles & Blazing Bargains , and VIP perks —stay tuned via our Loyalty VIP program!

 
 
 Your 4th‑of‑July Cannabis Checklist: 
 Pay us a visit before you hit the beach or parade.

 Dive into our summer bundles & VIP rewards .

 Take home your holiday essentials— flower , pre-rolls , edibles , vaporizers , concentrates , tinctures , CBD , accessories , and more.

 Enjoy a safe, happy, and elevated Independence Day—Cape Cod Cannabis style and celebrate responsibly! 

 
 
 
 Let Freedom—and Good Times—Blaze! 
 This 4th of July, set yourself up for a perfect Cape Cod celebration—with parades, beaches, baseball and fireworks—and stop by Cape Cod Cannabis Recreational Dispensary to complete the experience. From sunrise strolls to star-lit displays, we’ve got the holiday cannabis essentials to make your weekend unforgettable.
 
 See you in Wellfleet—Happy Independence Day! Celebrate responsibly.

pages.bodyText:
Terpene & Cannabinoid Guide

 What is a Terpene? What is a Cannabinoid? What is the Entourage Effect? Cape Cod Cannabis offers our Terpene & Cannabinoid Guide to help explain what terpenes and cannabinoids are, where they come from and how they interact with other compounds to form the entourage effect along with the potential benefits. Click on sections below for more information. 

 
 
 
 LEARN ABOUT TERPENES
 
 
 
 
 What is a Terpene and where does it come from in the cannabis plant?

 Terpenes are a large and diverse class of organic compounds produced by a variety of plants, including cannabis, conifers, and citrus trees. They are responsible for the distinctive flavors and aromas of many plants and have been used in traditional medicine for their potential therapeutic effects. In plants, terpenes serve several functions, including attracting pollinators and repelling predators.
 
 In the context of cannabis, terpenes are often associated with the plant’s aromatic profile, commonly referred to as the “terpene profile” or “terpene profile.” Cannabis strains can have different terpene profiles, contributing to the unique scent and flavor of each strain. Some common terpenes found in cannabis include:
 
 Myrcene : Known for its earthy and musky aroma, myrcene is believed to have relaxing and sedative effects. It’s also found in hops, mangoes, and lemongrass.
 Limonene : This terpene has a citrusy scent and is found in citrus fruits. Limonene is associated with potential mood-enhancing and stress-relieving effects.
 Pinene : As the name suggests, pinene has a pine-like aroma. It’s found in pine trees and is believed to have anti-inflammatory properties. There are two types of pinene: alpha-pinene and beta-pinene.

 Linalool : Linalool has a floral scent and is present in lavender, mint, and cinnamon. It is associated with potential relaxing and anti-anxiety effects.

 Humulene : With an earthy and woody aroma, humulene is found in hops, sage, and ginseng. It is sometimes considered to have anti-inflammatory properties.

 Caryophyllene : This terpene has a spicy and peppery aroma and is found in black pepper, cloves, and cinnamon. Caryophyllene is unique because it can also interact with cannabinoid receptors in the body’s endocannabinoid system.

 
 A good terpene percentage in cannabis that supports the entourage effect typically falls within the range of 1% to 4% of the total weight of the flower or concentrate. Here’s a breakdown:
 
 1–2% total terpenes : Mild aroma/flavor and moderate contribution to the entourage effect.

 2–4% total terpenes : Considered a robust terpene profile—often associated with enhanced effects, stronger aroma, and greater synergy with cannabinoids like THC and CBD.

 4%+ : Quite high—typically found in well-cured, premium flower or live resin products. These can deliver a very noticeable entourage effect.

 
 Terpenes are not unique to cannabis; they are present in a wide range of plants and contribute to the overall sensory experience of various fruits, flowers, and herbs. In addition to their role in aroma and flavor, terpenes are being studied for their potential therapeutic properties, both individually and in conjunction with cannabinoids like THC and CBD.
 
 Terpenes in the cannabis plant, like in many other plants, are produced in the glandular trichomes. Trichomes are small, hair-like structures that are most concentrated on the flowers (buds) of the cannabis plant, but they can also be found on other parts of the plant, including the leaves and stems. 
 
 There are more than 100 different terpenes that have been identified in cannabis. Each cannabis strain has a unique combination and concentration of terpenes, contributing to its distinct aroma, flavor, and potentially influencing its effects. While some terpenes are more commonly found in certain strains, the overall terpene profile can vary widely.
 
 The glandular trichomes contain resin glands that produce a mixture of cannabinoids (such as THC and CBD) and terpenes. Terpenes are synthesized in these glands through the same metabolic pathways that produce cannabinoids. The combination of cannabinoids and terpenes in the resin glands gives cannabis its distinctive aroma, flavor, and potential therapeutic effects.
 
 During the flowering stage of the cannabis plant’s life cycle, trichome production increases, and the terpene content becomes more prominent. As the plant matures, the concentration and composition of terpenes can change. Factors such as genetics, growing conditions, and environmental factors also influence the terpene profile of a cannabis strain.
 
 Harvesting and processing methods can impact the preservation of terpenes. Some methods, such as low-temperature drying and careful handling of the plant material, are employed to retain the maximum terpene content in the final product. Additionally, the extraction of essential oils from cannabis, often used in the production of concentrates and extracts, can isolate and concentrate terpenes for various applications.

 What is a Cannabinoid? 

 
 
 
 LEARN ABOUT CANNABINOIDS
 
 
 
 
 What is a Cannabinoid and where does it come from in the cannabis plant?

 Cannabinoids are naturally occurring compounds found in the cannabis plant. These chemical substances interact with the body’s endocannabinoid system (ECS) —a complex cell-signaling network that helps regulate vital functions like: 
 
 Mood

 Appetite

 Sleep

 Pain perception

 Memory

 Immune function

 
 There are over 100 known cannabinoids , each with its own effects and potential benefits. The most well-known cannabinoids are THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and CBD (cannabidiol) , but the cannabis plant contains many others worth exploring.
 
 How Cannabinoids Work in the Body 
 The endocannabinoid system (ECS) has two primary receptors:
 
 CB1 receptors : Found mainly in the brain and central nervous system

 CB2 receptors : Found in the immune system and peripheral organs

 
 Cannabinoids interact with these receptors to help maintain homeostasis—or balance—within the body.
 
 Natural and Synthetic Cannabinoids 
 Phytocannabinoids : Naturally produced by the cannabis plant

 Endocannabinoids : Produced by the human body (e.g., anandamide)

 Synthetic cannabinoids : Lab-created compounds that mimic natural cannabinoids, such as:
 Marinol (Dronabinol) – This is a pharmaceutical-grade synthetic THC used to treat nausea and vomiting in chemotherapy patients and to stimulate appetite in people with AIDS. It’s FDA-approved and taken orally in capsule form.

 Cesamet (Nabilone) – Another prescription synthetic cannabinoid, Cesamet is used for treating severe nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy. Like Marinol, it’s formulated to mimic THC but has a slightly different chemical structure.
 

 
 Choosing the Right Product 
 Cannabinoid-based products come in a wide range of forms. Depending on your goals, you might prefer:
 
 Flower – Full-spectrum, fast-acting

 Pre-Rolls – Convenient, portable, fast-acting
 Vapes – Convenient, portable, quick onset

 Tinctures – Precise dosing, discreet use

 Edibles – Longer-lasting effects

 Concentrates – Highly potent extracts like wax, shatter, live resin, rosin , and distillate 
 Ideal for experienced users seeking stronger, faster effects

 Used for dabbing , vape cartridges , or infusing other products 

 
 Topicals – Targeted, non-psychoactive relief

 CBD Products – Available in oils, capsules, gummies, topicals , and beverages 
 Non-intoxicating and widely used for stress, anxiety, inflammation , and general wellness 

 Perfect for daytime use or those looking to avoid THC

 
 
 Pro tip: Always start low and go slow , especially when trying THC-rich products.

 What is the cannabis Entourage Effect? 

 
 
 The entourage effect is a concept in cannabis pharmacology that suggests that the combination of various compounds found in the cannabis plant, including cannabinoids and terpenes, works together synergistically to produce a collective therapeutic effect that is greater than the sum of their individual effects. In other words, the interaction between different components of the cannabis plant may enhance or modify the overall therapeutic outcomes.
 
 The entourage effect is often used to explain why whole-plant extracts or full-spectrum cannabis products, which contain a broader range of cannabinoids and terpenes, may have different or more pronounced effects compared to isolated compounds (e.g., pure THC or CBD). Proponents of the entourage effect argue that the presence of multiple cannabinoids and terpenes in their natural ratios may create a more balanced and effective therapeutic outcome.
 
 Here are some key components involved in the entourage effect: 
 
 1. Cannabinoids : THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and CBD (cannabidiol) are the most well-known cannabinoids, but there are many others present in the cannabis plant, each with its potential effects.
 
 2. Terpenes : These aromatic compounds contribute to the flavor and scent of cannabis and may have their own therapeutic properties. The combination of specific terpenes with cannabinoids is thought to influence the overall experience and effects.
 
 3. Flavonoids: These are another group of compounds found in cannabis (as well as in many other plants) that have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Flavonoids may also contribute to the entourage effect.
 
 Research on the entourage effect is still ongoing, and the mechanisms behind how different compounds interact in the body are complex and not fully understood. While some studies support the idea of the entourage effect, more research is needed to determine its extent and significance in different therapeutic applications.
 
 It’s important to note that individual responses to cannabis can vary, and what works well for one person may not have the same effects for another. The entourage effect is a topic of interest in the field of medical cannabis, as researchers and clinicians seek to optimize therapeutic outcomes and understand the complexities of the plant’s chemical composition.
 
 Who coined the phrase “Entourage Effect”? 
 The term “entourage effect” was coined by Israeli scientists Raphael Mechoulam and S. Ben-Shabat in 1998. Raphael Mechoulam is a renowned organic chemist who is often referred to as the “father of cannabis research.” Mechoulam, along with his colleague S. Ben-Shabat, published a paper in the European Journal of Pharmacology titled “An entourage effect: inactive endogenous fatty acid glycerol esters enhance 2-arachidonoyl-glycerol cannabinoid activity.”
 
 In this seminal paper, Mechoulam and Ben-Shabat proposed the concept of the entourage effect, suggesting that the combined action of various compounds in the cannabis plant, including cannabinoids and terpenes, might produce a more significant and synergistic effect than the effects of individual compounds in isolation. They specifically explored how certain fatty acid glycerol esters enhanced the activity of the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoyl-glycerol.
 
 The entourage effect has since become a widely discussed and researched concept in the field of cannabis pharmacology. It has implications for understanding the therapeutic potential of whole-plant cannabis extracts, where multiple cannabinoids and terpenes are present in their natural ratios. The idea is that these compounds work together to create a more balanced and effective therapeutic outcome compared to isolated cannabinoids or synthetic compounds.

 Shop Cannabis Terpenes For Sale in Wellfleet, MA

 Discover the Power of Terpenes at Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet, MA. Terpenes are the aromatic compounds in cannabis that do more than just smell good—they play a key role in the effects and therapeutic benefits of each strain. At Cape Cod Cannabis , we help you understand how terpenes like myrcene, limonene, pinene, and linalool contribute to relaxation, energy, focus, or pain relief. Visit our Wellfleet dispensary to explore how terpenes enhance your cannabis experience and find the right product for your wellness goals.

 
 
 
 WHAT ARE TERPENES?
 
 
 
 
 Terpenes are a large and diverse class of organic compounds produced by a variety of plants, including cannabis, conifers, and citrus trees. They are responsible for the distinctive flavors and aromas of many plants and have been used in traditional medicine for their potential therapeutic effects. In plants, terpenes serve several functions, including attracting pollinators and repelling predators.
 In the context of cannabis, terpenes are often associated with the plant’s aromatic profile, commonly referred to as the “terpene profile” or “terpene profile.” Cannabis strains can have different terpene profiles, contributing to the unique scent and flavor of each strain. 
 
 In the context of cannabis, “primary” and “secondary” terpenes refer to their concentration and influence on a strain’s characteristics, specifically its taste, aroma, and effects. Primary terpenes are the most dominant and play a significant role in shaping a strain’s profile, while secondary terpenes contribute in smaller amounts, adding layers and nuances to the overall experience. 
 
 Terpenes are not unique to cannabis; they are present in a wide range of plants and contribute to the overall sensory experience of various fruits, flowers, and herbs. In addition to their role in aroma and flavor, terpenes are being studied for their potential therapeutic properties, both individually and in conjunction with cannabinoids like THC and CBD.
 
 A good terpene percentage in cannabis that supports the entourage effect typically falls within the range of 1% to 4% of the total weight of the flower or concentrate. Here’s a breakdown:
 1–2% total terpenes : Mild aroma/flavor and moderate contribution to the entourage effect.

 2–4% total terpenes : Considered a robust terpene profile—often associated with enhanced effects, stronger aroma, and greater synergy with cannabinoids like THC and CBD.

 4%+ : Quite high—typically found in well-cured, premium flower or live resin products. These can deliver a very noticeable entourage effect.

 The Ancient Origins of Halloween October 31st and our Toke or Treat

 
 
 
 
 
 October 23, 2025 
 
 

 Home / Cape Cod Lifestyle / The Ancient Origins of Halloween October 31st and our Toke or Treat 
 

 How Halloween Started: The Origins of Spooky Season
 Halloween, a holiday loved by millions around the world, has become a celebration of all things spooky, with costumes, candy, and haunted houses taking center stage. But how did Halloween, as we know it today, actually begin? Let’s take a journey through time to explore the origins of Halloween and how it transformed into the festive and spooky holiday we love today.
 
 The Ancient Origins of Halloween
 Halloween dates back over 2,000 years to the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain (pronounced “sow-win”) . The Celts, who lived in what is now Ireland, the UK, and northern France, celebrated their new year on November 1st. This date marked the end of summer and the harvest, as well as the beginning of the cold, dark winter, a time often associated with death.
 
 On the night of October 31st, the Celts believed that the boundary between the living and the dead was blurred, and that ghosts of the dead returned to earth. To ward off these spirits, they would light bonfires and wear costumes to protect themselves from evil.
 
 As Christianity spread throughout the Celtic lands, the church incorporated elements of Samhain into their own traditions. By the 9th century, the church designated November 1st as All Saints’ Day , a day to honor saints and martyrs. The night before, All Hallows’ Eve , eventually became what we now call Halloween… or as we like to say, “Halloweed” .
 
 Halloween Comes to America
 When European immigrants, especially the Irish fleeing the potato famine in the 1800s, came to America, they brought their Halloween customs with them. Over time, these customs merged with other traditions, like Native American harvest celebrations and British “Guy Fawkes Day.” By the late 19th century, Halloween had become a community-based holiday in the U.S., marked by parties, parades, and trick-or-treating.
 
 Trick-or-treating has its roots in the medieval tradition of “souling,” where the poor would go door-to-door offering prayers for the dead in exchange for food. In America, by the 1930s and 40s, this evolved into the child-friendly custom we know today, where kids dress up in costumes and go door-to-door collecting candy.
 
 Modern-Day Halloween: Fun for All Ages
 Today, Halloween is more than just a day for kids to collect sweets. It’s a celebration enjoyed by people of all ages, with costume parties, haunted attractions, and an abundance of spooky-themed events. Whether you’re into ghost stories, horror films, or simply carving pumpkins, Halloween offers something for everyone.
 
 As October 31st approaches, it’s the perfect time to embrace the festive spirit by decorating your home, preparing your costume, and yes, indulging in some seasonal treats.
 
 
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis “Toke or Treat” Bundles
 Speaking of treats, Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet is getting into the Halloween (Halloweed) spirit with our Toke or Treat Bundles . These exclusive bundles are perfect for cannabis enthusiasts looking to add a little extra fun to their Halloween celebrations. Whether you’re planning a spooky movie night, a Halloween-themed party, or just enjoying a quiet evening at home, our Toke or Treat Bundles provide everything you need to enhance your experience.
 
 Cape Cod Cannabis Toke or Treat Bundles come packed with a variety of premium cannabis products, from pre-rolls to edibles, ensuring you’ll have a range of options to elevate your Halloween festivities. Stop by our Wellfleet location, in the Rt. 6 shopping plaza, to grab your Toke or Treat bundle and celebrate Halloweed Cape Cod style !
 
 Celebrate Halloweed with a Twist!
 Halloween is a time for fun, frights, and a bit of mischief. Whether you’re hosting a party, trick-or-treating, or just enjoying the spooky season, Cape Cod Cannabis has you covered. Our Toke or Treat Bundles are the perfect companion for any Halloween celebration for everyone 21 yrs or older. So, while you’re embracing the ghosts of Halloween’s past, make sure to stop by and treat yourself to something special! And, as always, celebrate responsibly.
 
 
 ——
 
 Looking for more information on how to celebrate Halloweed with Cape Cod Cannabis? Visit our store in Wellfleet or check out our website for all the latest offerings and always celebrate responsibly.

 The Ins and Outs of Vaping

 
 
 
 
 
 January 2, 2022 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / The Ins and Outs of Vaping 
 

 The Ins and Outs of Vaping
 Vaping is a very popular way of consuming cannabis, mostly because of how discreet and convenient it is. Users can vape inside their home without worrying about creating a lingering odor like smoking does. I personally don’t find the effects to be as potent as smoking, but it’s nice to be able to get high from bed without stepping outside into the New England winter. If you’re considering getting into vaping, I recommend getting a disposable vape pen from your local dispensary to try it out. Disposables are nice because you don’t have to keep up with charging the battery and you simply throw the whole thing away once you’ve exhausted all the oil inside. No commitment, no hassle. Sometimes there’s a button to hold down while using it, others will be automatically activated by you just inhaling. If you’ve tried vaping already and like it, it may be time to make the switch to cartridges. Cartridges will require you to invest in your own battery to heat the oil up, but it will pay itself off eventually as you typically save a little bit of money per cartridge in comparison to disposables. Let’s explore a few commonly asked questions regarding vapes.
 
 Disposables have been working great for me. Is it really worth looking into cartridges? 
 If you prefer the convenience of a disposable, then by all means stick with them. I only recommend switching for three main reasons. The first reason is that it can be a bit wasteful to throw away an entire disposable every time. They each contain a lithium-ion battery that can degrade overtime and leak chemicals. The second reason is that there are usually a lot more options for cartridges compared to disposables. Lastly, as stated earlier, you will save money in the long run. Where I live, you can get 0.5ml carts as cheap as $50 and smaller 0.3ml disposables around $40. This seemingly small price variance can add up pretty quickly over time.
 
 How long do disposables/cartridges last? 
 There’s a few factors that will affect how quickly you go through a vape so it’s hard to say for sure. Some people take longer hits than others and some take hits more frequently. If you’re someone who just takes a few puffs each night before bed, a 0.5ml cart could last a couple weeks. Heavy users could easily go through that in a day.
 
 Isn’t vaping dangerous? I remember hearing about people suddenly dying from vapes a couple years ago. 
 The influx in vape-related deaths within the last couple years has been a result of people using illegal vapes they purchased off the black market. These vapes were being cut with vitamin E acetate to make the oil last longer, which can be deadly when inhaled. Each state that allows the sales of marijuana is very involved in the regulation of goods from dispensaries so there’s no risk of vitamin E acetate being present in your legal purchases.
 
 How do I know I’m getting the right kind of cartridge/battery? 
 There’s a few different options for cartridges and their battery counterparts in the cannabis industry. The most common by far are 510 threaded. 510 thread carts will have a circular connector piece that screws into any brand of 510 battery. Pretty much every single dispensary in the country will have these carts abundantly available. Other cartridge options I’ve seen are Pax pods and Dart pods. The Pax pod is rectangle-shaped and only fits into a Pax Era brand battery. Dart pods feature a dome-shaped magnetic pod that only fits into a CCELL Dart battery. Some individuals find certain features of Pax or Dart to be ideal for them specifically, otherwise most people prefer 510 threaded products due to availability and the opportunity to get any 510 battery of your choosing.
 
 What battery should I buy? 
 For 510 thread batteries, the options are endless. Just know you sort of get what you pay for when it comes to batteries. You could spend as little as $5 on one, but it likely won’t last a year. Others spend up to $100 or more for batteries that are super durable and high quality. I find the sweet spot to be around $20. I have plenty of batteries around this price point that I’ve had for more than two years now. I personally like the brand Yocan, due to the consistency and durability without breaking the bank.
 
 What is the difference between an oil vape and a dry-herb vape? 
 Everything previously mentioned in this article has been an oil vape. These are vapes that are pre-loaded with an oil, such as distillate. Dry herb vapes are vaporizers with an empty chamber for you to load with actual flower. Vaping flower provides a full-spectrum experience, where the taste and effects of the original flower strain will remain intact (unlike distillate).
 
 Taylor Sieg – CCC Product Specialist

 The Myth of High THC Potency: Why It’s Not the Only Factor in Choosing the Best Cannabis Flower

 
 
 
 
 
 October 1, 2024 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / The Myth of High THC Potency: Why It’s Not the Only Factor in Choosing the Best Cannabis Flower 
 

 The Myth of High THC Potency: Why It’s Not the Only Factor in Choosing the Best Cannabis Flower 
 When shopping for cannabis flower, many people believe that high THC potency is the most important factor in determining quality and effect. It’s easy to see why—THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the primary psychoactive compound in cannabis, so it’s often assumed that more THC equals a stronger and better experience. However, at Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet, MA , we’re here to dispel the myth that high THC alone determines the best cannabis flower.
 
 While THC levels play a role in the overall potency, there’s much more to the cannabis experience than just the percentage on the label. Factors like terpene profiles, cannabinoids, and how the plant was grown all contribute to the unique effects, flavors, and benefits of each strain . Focusing solely on THC can lead consumers to miss out on some of the most enjoyable and beneficial aspects of cannabis.
 
 Terpenes: The Aromatic Powerhouses 
Terpenes are aromatic compounds found in cannabis that influence its scent, taste, and effects. They work synergistically with THC and other cannabinoids in what’s called the “entourage effect.” This interaction helps enhance the overall experience of the strain, contributing to effects like relaxation, focus, or even creativity. Strains with rich terpene profiles can deliver a more balanced and enjoyable experience, regardless of the THC percentage. Visit our Terpene Guide for more information.
 
 
 
 For instance, a strain high in the terpene myrcene may offer deep relaxation and pain relief, while limonene might uplift and energize. These terpene combinations can make a strain with moderate THC levels feel more potent or effective than a high-THC strain with a weaker terpene profile.
 
 The Importance of Cannabinoids 
Beyond THC, cannabis contains over 100 other cannabinoids, such as CBD, CBG, and CBN, each with its own set of therapeutic properties. A strain with a balanced cannabinoid profile might provide a more nuanced, less overwhelming high than a strain that’s THC-heavy but lacking in other cannabinoids. For example, strains with higher levels of CBD can help mitigate anxiety or paranoia that can sometimes accompany high-THC strains, creating a more comfortable and enjoyable experience.
 
 Cultivation Quality Matters 
The way cannabis is cultivated also plays a significant role in the final product’s quality. At Cape Cod Cannabis, we focus on sourcing flower from trusted growers who prioritize sustainable and organic growing practices. Properly grown cannabis tends to have better flavor, smoother smoke, and more consistent effects. Even a high-THC strain can disappoint if it’s poorly grown, lacking in flavor and balance.
 
 Finding the Best Flower at Cape Cod Cannabis 
At Cape Cod Cannabis, we believe in educating our customers to look beyond THC potency and explore the many factors that make a cannabis flower exceptional. We carry a wide selection of strains that vary in THC levels but shine in terms of terpene richness, cannabinoid content, and overall quality. Our knowledgeable staff is here to help you find the right flower for your needs, whether you’re seeking relaxation, creativity, or relief.
 
 Remember, the best cannabis flower isn’t always about having the highest THC percentage. Instead, it’s about finding the right balance of effects, flavor, and overall enjoyment. Explore our wide range of strains at Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet, MA, and discover a whole new way to experience cannabis.

 Ready to learn more and find the perfect strain for you? Stop by Cape Cod Cannabis in the Route 6 shopping plaza in South Wellfleet , and talk to our expert team of product specialists. We’re here to guide you through the wide world of cannabis, so you can discover the right products for your lifestyle and needs. Plus, don’t forget to check out our blog for more insights on cannabis myths and information, strain reviews, and tips for enjoying the best cannabis experience possible.

 The Perks of a Dry Herb Vaporizer

 
 
 
 
 
 January 23, 2022 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / The Perks of a Dry Herb Vaporizer 
 

 The Perks of a Dry Herb Vaporizer
 As much as I love my joints, bowls, and bong rips, I will always be a huge advocate for dry herb vaporizers. I had my first experience with one in college where my friends and I had to be extremely discreet with our cannabis usage in the dorms. The Pax 2 that we all shared was perfect for getting high without sounding off the smoke alarms or stinking up the hallways. Although we used it for it’s inconspicuousness, I quickly fell in love with all the aspects of vaping flower. If you’re considering investing in a dry herb vape, I implore you to consider all of these great perks.
 
 Although cannabis itself has many health benefits, inhaling any kind of smoke is not good for you or your lungs. A vape will heat flower up enough to activate the desired cannabinoids whilst stopping any actual combustion from taking place. Studies show that dry herb vape users have significantly decreased respiratory symptoms compared to smokers.
 As previously mentioned, it’s great for users looking to remain discreet. Because you’re producing vapor instead of smoke, the odor dissipates quickly. This can be ideal for students, parents, and anyone else looking to keep their cannabis use confidential.
 The high produced from vaping cannabis is a much different experience than smoking it. I can only describe it as being more of a clear-headed, functional high. Some people really love it, while others don’t. I’m personally a fan of it.
 Already vaped bud (AVB) is one of the best things about dry herb vapes. Vaping your flower at low temperatures will mean that you still have some viable, decarboxylated herb in the chamber when you’re done with it. You can use this stuff to get high again. You can make some edibles with it or simply eat it straight up. I like putting some on a cracker with peanut butter to mask the unpleasant taste.
 
 Taylor Sieg – CCC Product Specialist

 The Ultimate 420 Dabbing Temperature Guide for Concentrates and Terpenes

 
 
 
 
 
 October 16, 2024 
 
 

 Home / Cannabis 101 / The Ultimate 420 Dabbing Temperature Guide for Concentrates and Terpenes 
 

 The Ultimate Dabbing Temperature Guide for Concentrates and Terpenes: A Cape Cod Cannabis Guide
 At Cape Cod Cannabis in Wellfleet , we believe the key to a perfect dabbing experience lies in choosing the right temperature. Whether you’re dabbing shatter , wax , live resin , or rosin , your temperature can unlock or suppress the flavor and potency of your concentrates. Our guide will help you find the optimal temperature for your needs, from preserving terpenes to achieving the most potent hit.
 
 Why Dabbing Temperature Matters
 Dabbing involves heating cannabis concentrates to vaporize cannabinoids and terpenes without burning them. The temperature you use affects both the taste and the effect, offering a range of experiences from smooth and flavorful to intense and powerful.
 Take a look at the image below, which breaks down optimal temperature ranges for different types of dabs, and highlights when specific terpenes and cannabinoids vaporize:
 
 
 
 This chart gives you a visual reference for understanding how different temperatures impact the flavor and potency of your concentrates.
 
 Low-Temperature Dabbing
 Low-temp dabs (as shown in the image, between 400°F and 500°F) are perfect for those who prioritize flavor. Many delicate terpenes vaporize at this range, such as Limonene (349°F / 176°C) and Myrcene (334°F / 168°C), which provide citrusy and earthy flavors, respectively. This range delivers a smooth hit with more nuanced flavors but lower vapor production and potency.
 
 Best for: 
 Concentrates high in terpenes like live resin and sauce
 Flavor-focused users
 Key Terpenes Activated at Low Temps: 
 Limonene: 349°F / 176°C
 Myrcene: 334°F / 168°C
 Linalool: 388°F / 198°C
 Pros: 
 Maximum flavor preservation
 Smooth on the throat and lungs
 Cons: 
 Less vapor production
 Less intense effects
 
 Medium-Temperature Dabbing
 Mid-range dabs (500°F – 545°F) offer a balance between flavor and vapor production. In this range, both terpenes and cannabinoids are more fully activated, leading to a richer experience in terms of effects and taste. Cannabinoids like CBD and THC begin to fully vaporize in this range, maximizing potency while still offering a decent flavor profile.
 
 Best for: 
 Those who want a balanced experience of flavor and potency
 Shatter, wax, and budder
 Key Cannabinoids and Terpenes Activated at Medium Temps: 
 THC: 315°F / 157°C
 CBD: 356°F / 180°C
 Pinene: 311°F / 155°C
 Pros: 
 Good balance of flavor and potency
 Suitable for a wide range of concentrates
 Cons: 
 Some loss of terpene flavor compared to lower temps
 Vapor is warmer and may be harsher
 
 High-Temperature Dabbing
 For those seeking intense effects, high-temp dabs (570°F – 600°F) are ideal. At these temperatures, cannabinoids like THC and CBD fully vaporize, offering potent hits and thick vapor clouds. However, many terpenes are burned off, resulting in less flavor. If you’re prioritizing potency over flavor, this range is for you.
 
 Best for: 
 Users seeking immediate, intense effects
 Heavy-duty concentrates like diamonds and distillates
 Key Terpenes Activated at High Temps: 
 Humulene: 388°F / 198°C
 Caryophyllene: 266°F / 130°C
 Pros: 
 Maximum potency and vapor production
 Great for heavy concentrates
 Cons: 
– Loss of terpene flavor
– Harsh on the throat and lungs
 
 Recap of Temperature Ranges
 To make things easier, here’s a quick summary of temperature ranges based on your goals:
 
 Low-temp dabs (400°F – 500°F): Best for maximizing flavor and terpenes like Linalool, Limonene, and Myrcene.
 Mid-range dabs (500°F – 545°F): Great for a balanced hit with good flavor and potency.
 High-temp dabs (570°F – 600°F): Ideal for users looking for intense effects and heavy vapor production, though flavor is reduced.
 
 Tips for Dabbing Success
 Use a Carb Cap : Helps maintain even heat and vaporization, improving the overall experience.
 Clean Your Rig Regularly: Residue affects flavor, so clean your rig to preserve the taste of your dabs.
 Invest in Quality Tools : Tools like a good e-nail or thermometer help maintain consistent temperatures and avoid burning your concentrates.
 
 At Cape Cod Cannabis , we offer a wide range of concentrates that suit every preference. Whether you’re after flavorful live resin or potent diamonds, our team can guide you toward the best products for your dabbing setup. Visit us in Wellfleet, in the Rt. 6 Shopping Plaza, to discover high-quality concentrates and the perfect tools to enhance your dabbing experience!
